tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__delete_session
tools.description:
Delete CCD sessions. Each session's transcript, record and worktree (with its branch) are removed and cannot be recovered — archive_session is the reversible alternative, so prefer it unless the user explicitly asked to delete.

Up to 25 session_ids per call. The app shows the user one approval card that lists every session by title, in every permission mode (auto and bypass permissions included), and nothing is deleted until they approve it. From a session on a remote (SSH) host only an approval in the Claude app on the user's computer counts, not one from another device. Never this session. A session that is working, still starting, pinned, open on the user's screen, or whose worktree another live session is working in is skipped, and so is one whose worktree has uncommitted changes, could not be checked, or lives on a remote host — unless force_worktree_cleanup is true, which discards that work; pass it only after telling the user, in your own message, which sessions' uncommitted changes will be lost (the card shows the flag). A deleted session's side sessions are archived (not deleted) with it, except those still at work, which stay live under the session above it; a branch holding commits that exist nowhere else is kept (on a remote host the branch is always left in place). The result names what was deleted, what was archived with it, which side sessions stayed live, and what was skipped and why. Unavailable in unattended sessions.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_session
tools.description:
Get detailed metadata for a single CCD session by ID, or for this session with "self".

Returns the same fields as a list_sessions entry (including the sidebar `group` and `pinned`, which the ccd_sidebar tools change when available, `link` and `remoteControlActive`) plus creation time, model, effort, permission mode (`permissionMode`, reported for this session and sessions this session started only), fast mode (`fastMode`: the state the session last reported — on, off or cooldown — and, when something blocks it, why; omitted until its process has reported), output style (`outputStyle`: the style its process last reported, "default" for none; like `permissionMode` reported for this session and sessions this session started only, and omitted until the process has reported — set_session_output_style changes it), worktree/branch info, whether the session is remote, scheduled-task linkage, agent, `remoteControlState` ("on", "off", "connecting", or "unavailable" where the app cannot bridge that session) with `startedViaRemoteControl` when a phone or claude.ai started the session (its Remote Control switch is then locked), and — for a session started from another — `parentSessionId` with `detached` (true once it was moved to top level). Metadata only — no conversation content (use list_events for that). Use this when you have a session_id and want its full configuration without re-listing everything, or to learn this session's own title, permission mode, sidebar group or link.

`link` opens the session in this app from outside it — use it in text that leaves this conversation (a PR description, Slack, a file); in your replies here, link a session as [its title](#<sessionId>) instead. Omitted when the organization turned app links off.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_usage
tools.description:
The account's Claude Code plan limits and how full a session's context window is.

`plan`: the limits the app's usage card shows (5-hour, weekly, per-model weekly, extra usage) with percent used and reset time. For pacing side sessions and deciding when to wrap up, compact or hand off. Read-only.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__list_sessions
tools.description:
List the user's other CCD sessions (active and optionally archived).

Returns a compact JSON array sorted by most recent activity. The current session is excluded. Use this to answer "what other sessions do I have", to find a session by title/branch/PR/sidebar group, or — after a PR you opened has merged — to locate the corresponding session and offer to archive it via archive_session.

`permissionMode` (default, acceptEdits, plan, auto or bypassPermissions) is reported only for sessions this session started; other rows omit it. A linked session (one Claude started from another with start_session, or a linked fork) also carries `name` — the short handle its family calls it by — and `startedBy`, the id of the session that started it; pass {"linked": true} to list only your own family. `group` is the custom sidebar group the user filed a session under ({id, name}), or null when it is ungrouped. The key is omitted while the app window has not reported groups yet — treat that as unknown, not ungrouped. `pinned` is true or false per the sidebar pin (a pinned session keeps its group but is shown under Pinned); the key is omitted when the app has never recorded a pin for the session — read that as not pinned. To change either, use the ccd_sidebar tools when they are available (move_sessions, set_pinned, create_group, ...).

`link` opens the session in this app from outside it — use it in text that leaves this conversation (a PR description, Slack, a file); in your replies here, link a session as [its title](#<sessionId>) instead. Omitted when the organization turned app links off. `remoteControlActive` says Remote Control is serving the session to claude.ai/code (the user opens it from the Remote Control badge; its address is not given to you).

Pass include_archived: true to find archived sessions to restore (unarchive_session) or remove for good (delete_session, which asks the user first in every permission mode).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__send_message
tools.description:
Prefer `SendMessage` with `to` set to the target's `local_...` session id (the id, not its display name); this older tool stays callable for now.

Send a message to another CCD session. The message arrives in the target session as a user turn labelled "From {this session's title}" with a link back here, so the user can see where it came from.

The result says what actually happened: "delivered" means that session's turn has started on your message; "queued" means it is waiting behind that session's current work and runs when that finishes; anything else is an error saying why it was not delivered. Every result ends with "(delivery: ...; message_id: ...)".

Use it to hand off context, ask the other session to pick something up, or relay a finding — not to orchestrate background work. It cannot deliver into a session an orchestrator dispatched.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_model
tools.description:
Switch the model another CCD session uses, from its next turn on (a turn already in flight finishes on the current model). `model` must be one of the ids the app's model picker offers; when it is not, the result lists them.

Usually no prompt when the target is a session this session started and the model is this session's exact model or one from a cheaper family (a permission rule can still require one); a more expensive model, or any other session, and the app asks the user first (in auto mode it may decide without asking; in bypass permissions mode it does not ask). Refused for this session: a session must not silently re-price its own turns — if this session should run on a different model, ask the user to pick it in the model menu.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_output_style
tools.description: Switch the output style ONE Code session writes in ("self" or another session) — the session title-bar menu's Output style, from the session's next turn on: a built-in style (Explanatory, Learning, ...), "default" for none, or a custom style the user already has (the session's own list; an unknown name is refused and the result lists what can be set). It changes that session only and the user can switch it back from the same menu; the user's default style for NEW sessions is a preference — use the ccd_settings tools (set_setting output_style) for that, not this. The app asks the user first with a card naming the session and the old and new style (auto mode may decide without asking; bypass permissions never asks). Refused for a session whose Claude Code has not reported its styles yet (not started, or idle since a restart) and in unattended sessions. get_session reports a session's current style as `outputStyle`.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_permission_mode
tools.description: Switch a CCD session ("self" or another) to a permission mode: default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, bypassPermissions. Applies at once; for "self" the rest of this turn runs in the new mode. A switch to a mode that does MORE without asking (plan < default < acceptEdits < auto < bypassPermissions) shows the user an approval card in every permission mode and waits for it; from a remote (SSH) session only an approval in the Claude app on the user's computer counts. No card for the same or a lower mode on this session or one it started; for other sessions the app asks first (auto mode may decide; bypass permissions never asks). Unavailable modes are refused. Unavailable in unattended sessions.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_title
tools.description:
Rename a CCD session — another session, or this one.

Use it when the user asks to rename a session, or after a session's scope has clearly changed and the old title is misleading. If the user set the current title themselves, the app first asks them to approve the new one (not in bypass permissions mode, which does not ask; and in unattended sessions, where nobody can approve, it declines); titles the app generated are replaced without asking. When the request didn't come from the user, prefer renaming only sessions whose titles are clearly stale. A subagent can't rename the session it runs in.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__stop_session
tools.description:
Interrupt another CCD session's in-flight turn — the same as the user pressing Stop there. The session stays open and idle afterwards; a message already queued in it runs next.

Usually no prompt when the target is a session this session started (start_session / hand_off_to_session, or a task the user launched from one of this session's suggestions) — an admin or user permission rule can still require one; for any other session the app asks the user first (in auto mode it may decide without asking; in bypass permissions mode it does not ask). Not for this session — you end your own turn by finishing your reply. A session that is idle, still starting, or archived is left alone and the result says so.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__unarchive_session
tools.description:
Restore an archived CCD session to the session list. Its conversation is intact; a worktree removed at archive is recreated (remote host) or re-acquired on its next turn (local).

Usually no prompt when the target is a session this session started (start_session / hand_off_to_session, or a task the user launched from one of this session's suggestions) — an admin or user permission rule can still require one; for any other session the app asks the user first (in auto mode it may decide without asking; in bypass permissions mode it does not ask). Use it when the user asks to bring back a session they (or you, via archive_session) archived — find it with list_sessions include_archived: true. Not for this session (a running session is never archived). Unavailable in remote-dispatched sessions.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_settings__get_settings
tools.description: Read the user's Code tab preferences in this app: session auto-archiving, branch prefix, notifications, keep-awake, prompt suggestions, the Remote Control default for new sessions and the default output style. Each comes back with its current value, the values set_setting accepts, one line on what it does, and, when it can't be changed from here right now, why (locked). Also reports, read-only, facts you often need and can never change here: this session's default permission mode, whether bypass or auto mode is disabled by policy, the worktree location and whether Claude's browser tools are on. No approval is needed. Call it before set_setting, or when the user asks what their settings are.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_sidebar__set_view
tools.description:
Change how the Code-tab sidebar lists sessions — the same settings as its filter menu. Pass only the fields to change:
- group_by: "date" | "project" | "state" | "custom" | "none" ("project" groups by folder, or by environment where the sidebar lays sessions out in sections; "custom" is refused in that layout, whose groups are always their own sections; "state" needs the status filter at "active" and sets it)
- status: "active" | "archived" | "all" (only "active" where the sidebar lays sessions out in sections: archived sessions are on the Sessions page there, and another value is refused)
- sort_by: "recency" | "alpha" | "created" (recency = last activity, alpha = name, created = date created)
- last_activity: 0 | 1 | 3 | 7 | 30 days (0 = all; only applied while group_by is "state"; refused in the sections layout, which shows every age)
- section_id: optional, from list_sections. Absent or "sessions" changes the whole list as above. A section you or the user created ("manual") and the built-in section with id "routines" take their own group_by ("date" | "state" | "none"; "project" is refused there, it groups the whole column) and sort_by, and in the sections layout list their rows that way. The built-in section with id "pinned" saves group_by and sort_by but does not apply them to its list. status / last_activity are refused with any section_id but "sessions". The result carries section_shown: false when the user has that section switched off.
Returns the settings as they stand afterwards.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. tools.name: mcp__ccd_view__show_pane
tools.description:
Show one of this session's side panes in the user's view of the Claude desktop app, beside the conversation.

Panes: "diff" (the session's changes; optional `path` scrolls to that file, `diff_scope` picks all branch changes, uncommitted changes only, or one commit), "file" (`path` opens that file in the Files pane at `line`; must be inside the session's working directory or a folder the user granted), "terminal" (optional `tab_id` switches to that open tab), "pr" (the session's pull request), "tasks" (background tasks), "plan", "preview" (the Browser pane, once this session has a page open in it), "artifact" (the artifacts this session published). A page in a hidden Browser pane runs as a background page: animation may not run at all, and on some systems timers slow down once you haven't touched the page for a while. Showing the pane with that page's tab in front helps only while the Claude window is itself in view (not minimized or covered by another app), so don't rely on timing or performance numbers from the page unless the user is watching it.

Prefer showing over describing: after finishing a set of edits, show the diff; when pointing the user at code, open the file at the line. It only changes what is on screen for this session — if the session isn't open in any window it does nothing and says so (tell the user what to look at instead), and it never takes focus from another session. A pane in a window of its own is left where it is, never raised, reopened here or changed, and the result says so: tell the user to look there.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of browser tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — if an action navigates to a domain without permission, the next item's check fails and the batch stops. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

schema.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
schema.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__file_upload

Do not click on file upload buttons or file inputs — clicking opens a native file picker dialog that you cannot see or interact with. Instead, use read_page or find to locate the file input element, then use this tool with its ref to upload files directly. Pass `paths` of files this session can read (attachments, the session's working, outputs, or uploads folders, or folders the user has connected); a path the client's file-read permissions or the host does not allow is rejected. The combined size of all files in a single call must stay under 10 MB.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator
tools.description: Manage GIF recording and export for browser automation sessions. Control when to start/stop recording browser actions (clicks, scrolls, navigation), then export as an animated GIF with visual overlays (click indicators, action labels, progress bar, watermark). All operations are scoped to the tab's group. When starting recording, take a screenshot immediately after to capture the initial state as the first frame. When stopping recording, take a screenshot immediately before to capture the final state as the last frame. For export, either provide 'coordinate' to drag/drop upload to a page element, or set 'download: true' to download the GIF.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". tools.name: mcp__scheduled-tasks__create_scheduled_task
tools.description:
Create a scheduled task that runs automatically — on a recurring schedule or once at a future moment. Use this when the user asks for something to happen repeatedly ("every day at 6am", "each Monday", "hourly") or at a specific later time ("remind me in 20 minutes", "tomorrow at 3pm"), rather than once right now. Go ahead and call it when the request clearly describes a schedule; if the schedule or task content is ambiguous, confirm the details with the user first — an approval prompt may or may not appear depending on the user's permission settings, so don't rely on it as the confirmation step.

To modify an existing scheduled task's schedule or prompt, use `update_scheduled_task` instead.

The task is stored as {taskId}/SKILL.md in C:\Users\0xRay\.claude\scheduled-tasks/. Each run starts fresh with no memory of this conversation, so the prompt must be fully self-contained.

Scheduled tasks run while this app is open. If the app is closed when a task is due, it runs on next launch — tell the user this so they aren't surprised.

If the user chose Auto or Bypass permissions mode for this session, the task may be saved in that mode; the result says whether it was.

**Scheduling options (pick at most one):**
- cronExpression: recurring (daily, weekly, etc.) — a 5-field cron string in LOCAL time, not UTC
- fireAt: one-time (ISO 8601 timestamp with offset) — runs once at the given moment, then auto-disables. Never use a cron expression for a one-time task; cron has no one-shot semantics.
- Omit both: "ad-hoc" — can only be started manually

taskId.description: Kebab-case identifier for the task (e.g., 'check-inbox', 'daily-standup'). Used as the directory name and storage key. Auto-sanitized as a safety net. If that name is already in use on the user's computer the call is refused and, when another task's folder has it, names a free ID ('check-inbox-2') to call again with.

prompt.description: The full task prompt/instructions that will be executed each time the task runs. Write this as a complete prompt describing what Claude should do. Each run starts fresh with no memory of this conversation, so the prompt must be fully self-contained: include which connectors to use, the output format, and any preferences the user expressed here.

description.description: A short one-line description of what this task does (used in skill frontmatter).

cronExpression.description: Standard 5-field cron expression for recurring runs (minute hour dayOfMonth month dayOfWeek), evaluated in the user's LOCAL timezone, not UTC: use local times directly. '0 9 * * *' = every day at 9:00 AM; '0 9 * * 1-5' = weekdays at 9:00 AM; '30 8 * * 1' = every Monday at 8:30 AM; '0 0 1 * *' = the first day of every month at midnight. Recurring tasks apply a small deterministic delay of several minutes at dispatch time to balance server load. Mutually exclusive with fireAt.

fireAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone offset for a one-time run (e.g. '2026-03-05T14:30:00-08:00' runs once on March 5 at 2:30 PM Pacific). Use it for reminders ('remind me in 5 minutes'), one-off future actions ('tomorrow at 3pm') or specific dates. Must be in the future. The task fires once at that moment, with no load-balancing delay (or on next app launch if the app was closed), then disables itself. Mutually exclusive with cronExpression.

notifyOnCompletion.description: When true (default), this session receives a notification each time the task finishes a run. Pass false to opt out.

tools.description: Type a shell command into a tab of the user's Terminal panel (beside this conversation) and press Enter. The command runs in the user's interactive shell — PowerShell on their computer (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7, with their profile, aliases, PATH and credentials), or the host's login shell (zsh, bash or sh) in an SSH session — outside any sandbox, stays running after your turn ends, and its tab is added without opening the panel: the user can open the panel to watch it, type into it and stop it with Ctrl-C; you stop it, or close its tab when you are done with it, with stop_terminal_tab. Returns the tab's tab_id once the command is typed, which waits for the shell's startup files to finish (usually at once, longer for a slow shell); read what it printed with read_terminal {tab_id, wait_for_output_ms}. Prefer this over Bash for long-running or interactive things the user should see and control — dev servers, file watchers, test runners in watch mode, log tails, REPLs — and over preview_start for processes that are not an HTTP server to preview. Use Bash for short commands whose output you need in this turn. Each call opens a new tab, in cwd (default the session's working directory). `command` is one complete, literal command line in printable ASCII: commands, parameters, bare or quoted words, numbers, wildcards, comma lists, ; (and && / || on PowerShell 7), redirections, & or . before a quoted path, $true / $false / $null, and $env:NAME = 'value'. Refused before anything is typed, by PowerShell's own parser: anything computed (variable reads such as $x, $env:TEMP or "$x", pipes, ( ) / $( ) / @( ), script blocks, member access, casts, hashtables, if / foreach / function, --%), a comment and an incomplete line, reported with the parser's error; as any word on the line, Invoke-History / ihy / r, Invoke-Expression / iex, Add-Type, the alias cmdlets and sal / nal / ipal, New-PSDrive / ndr / mount, prompt and anything of PSReadLine's; the function:, alias: and env: drives, $env:PSModulePath, the words using and configuration standing alone, any backtick, more than one line, and control or non-ASCII characters. In an SSH session the host's zsh, bash or sh reads the line instead, with that shell's own refusals. Put anything more in a file (Write) and run the file here (& .\build.ps1). In default mode the user approves the exact line; in auto mode the classifier judges it as it would the same command run through Bash with the sandbox disabled, read as typed at an interactive prompt (in an SSH session the user is always asked, whatever the mode). In an SSH session the command is typed only when the host confirms nothing else is running in the new shell. A command that could not be typed is reported with the reason and what became of the tab.

14:- **R2-06, no evidence that high KL means high utility; the sum over $x\\in X$ is ill-defined.** @OK@ The sum is now explicit (Eqs. (5a), (5b), (5)). Three comparators were measured: the global cross-entropy of the client's examples (+0.64, +0.50, +0.75), a loss-based utility used for selection (accuracy difference to KL +0.57 [\u22120.33, +1.64] on CIFAR-10 and +0.25 [\u22120.08, +0.48] on FMNIST, i.e. not distinguishable), and the raw parameter drift $\\|w_i^t-w^t_{global}\\|$. KL correlates with the gain more strongly than the drift under the two-class-per-client split (CIFAR-10 +0.71 vs +0.33; FMNIST +0.75 vs +0.50; paired differences +0.37 [+0.32, +0.43] and +0.25 [+0.09, +0.46]) and not distinguishably otherwise (+0.17 [\u22120.17, +0.43]; \u22120.08 [\u22120.34, +0.11]). We therefore present KL as a valid and cheap label-free indicator, not as the optimal one.
15:- **R1-05, uncertainty penalty (also asked in Replacement 5's variance paragraph).** @OK@ The text states that the variance measures dispersion across scoring batches, that it does not by itself separate noise from heterogeneity, that $B\\ge 2$, and defines the sample variance. Evidence: it does not discriminate noisy clients (rank AUC 0.45 [0.39, 0.52], chance level); it is retained because removing it lowers accuracy by 0.54 [\u22120.80, \u22120.40] on CIFAR-10 and 0.68 [\u22120.93, \u22120.50] on FMNIST.
21:- **R1-02 and R2-04, ill-posed control law, wrong direction, $\\lambda$ unspecified, "Lyapunov".** @OK@ The denominator is $\\lambda F_i^t+|\\nu^t(\\Delta KL_i^t-F_i^t)|>0$; $\\lambda=1$ and $\\beta=0.9$ are stated; the direction is derived and the Lyapunov wording is removed. Evidence of the direction: when $\\nu^t>0$ the mean mixing coefficient fell in 96.7% of 1,827 rounds; the per-run Spearman correlation between $\\nu^t$ and the change of $a$ has median \u22120.72. Insensitive to $\\lambda$ ($\\lambda=10$: 85.07) and $\\beta$ ($\\beta=0.5$: 85.08) against 85.07 by default (FMNIST).

الملف جاهز: [FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx](FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx). أنشأته بقاعدة نص قبل/بعد مع مواضع التعديل داخل `sn-article.tex`. لم أفتحه في Word ولم أُجمّع ملف tex لأنه لا يوجد محرك TeX هنا.

**ما يحتويه:**
1. **جدول تغطية التعليقات.** يربط كل تعليق للمراجعين (R1-02, R1-04, R1-05, R2-04, R2-05, R2-06, R2-18, R2-20) بوسم ADDRESSED أو PARTIAL، مع الدليل التجريبي بجانبه.
2. **Replacement 5 و6 (قبل/بعد).** التعديلات بالمعادلات الأصلية (5a، 5b، 5، 12a، 12، 13، 14، 8، 9) مع تظليل الحذف والإضافة.
3. **ثلاث فقرات جاهزة للصق في Section 5.** الأولى لصلاحية مؤشر المنفعة KL، والثانية لعقوبة التباين، والثالثة لسلوك المعامل `a` والمقارنة بالقيم الثابتة. كُتبت بصيغة بحثية: النتيجة ثم الرقم ثم فاصل الثقة 95%، دون ادعاء.
4. **قائمة المخاطر.** الأسئلة التي قد يطرحها المراجع مع إجابة جاهزة لكل منها.

**ما تغيّر في النص بعد التجربتين الأخيرتين:**
- **المتحكم:** لم يعد يُقدَّم كمكوّن ثبتت أفضليته. نصّ R6 صار: "طريقة لضبط `a` تلقائياً، ولا نزعم تفوقها على ثابت مضبوط جيداً". المتحكم يتفوق فقط على `a=0.5` (+1.25 إلى +1.62 نقطة، وJFI من 0.934 إلى 0.997)، لكن `a=0.05` الثابت يساويه. المتحكم يُقدَّم كاختياري.
- **مؤشر KL:** أُضيف مقارنته بانجراف المعاملات. KL أقوى ارتباطاً بفائدة التحديث في حالتين (s2 على CIFAR-10 وFMNIST) ولا يختلف معنوياً في الحالتين الأخريين. أبقيته مؤشراً صالحاً وغير مكلف، لا الأفضل: الخسارة العالمية تساويه أو تتفوق عليه قليلاً.

**قيود يجب أن تبقى في الورقة:**
- دراسة انجراف المعاملات ببذرتين فقط (12 جولة-تشغيل لكل حالة)، ودراسة `a` الثابت بثلاث بذور، فالفواصل استدلالية.
- يجب أن تذكر الورقة أن كل الأرقام من إعادة تنفيذ.
- ترقيم "Table X/Y" و"5.x/5.y/5.z" عناوين مؤقتة تضبطها حسب جداول Section 5 عندك.

الخطوة التالية: صياغة الملخص والمساهمات والعنوان على نفس الأساس. أبدأها إن أردت.

نعم، جدولان مطلوبان من ملف 5 و6 نفسه، وجدول ثالث اختياري. كل الأرقام عندي من التجارب، ولم أنسّقها كجداول بعد.

**1. الجدول X: صلاحية مؤشر المنفعة** (يُشار إليه في 5.x)
- الأعمدة: السيناريو، وسبيرمان لـ KL، وللخسارة العالمية، ولانجراف المعاملات، وفاصل ثقة KL.
- الصفوف: ثلاثة سيناريوهات non-IID وسيناريو ضوضاء التسميات (S3).
- المتاح:
  - KL: +0.50 و+0.39 و+0.73، وتحت الضوضاء +0.12.
  - الخسارة العالمية: +0.64 و+0.50 و+0.75.
  - الانجراف: مقاس في سيناريوهين فقط (s1_0.1 وs2)، وغير مقاس في s1_0.5 وفي الضوضاء. اترك الخانات الناقصة "—" ولا تملأها.

**2. الجدول Y: المعامل `a` الثابت مقابل المتحكم** (يُشار إليه في 5.z)
- الأعمدة: الدقة، وJFI، ونسبة العملاء غير المختارين، وأقصى انتظار، وأضعف 10% من العملاء.
- الصفوف: المتحكم، و`a`=0.05 و0.10 و0.5 و1.
- الأرقام جاهزة للمتحكم و0.05 و0.10 و1 على FMNIST وCIFAR-10 (3 بذور). الصف `a`=0.5 ينقصه أقصى انتظار وأضعف 10%، فأحسبهما من نتائج `abl_fixmix`.

**3. جدول اختياري: سلوك `a`.** الوسيط 0.04، والمتوسط 0.10، والمئينان 5 و95 (0.005 و0.32). يكفي سطر في النص ولا يحتاج جدولاً.

**أرقام ناقصة خارج 5 و6 (لمن يقرأ الورقة كاملة):**
- جداول الدقة والإنصاف والتكلفة في Section 5 الرئيسي (Replacement 11): محتجزة بانتظار قرارك.
- Table 4 (F1 مقابل recall) وTable 5 (حد الكوهورت 10.17): لم تُعدَّل.

551	The evaluation of FedFACS was conducted across a range of heterogeneous data distribution conditions, with the experiments performed on a system using an Nvidia RTX 3090 GPU and 32 GB of RAM.
552	
553	The relative contribution of each component in FedFACS is individually evaluated through a comprehensive ablation study. The components are the full FedFACS, FedFACS-A1 which removes both of adaptive aggregation and cohort sizing (Ablation 1), where client selection is performed with a constant sampling size of ($C_k^t=10$) and static weighted aggregation is used (McMahan et al. 2017), and FedFACS-A2 that utilizing dynamic cohort sizing with ($C_{k_{\min}} = 8$) and ($C_{k_{\max}} = 10$) removes adaptive aggregation only (Ablation 2). The experimental setup follows configuration A, and The target accuracy is determined as the maximum accuracy obtained by FedAvg under the corresponding experiments with data partitioning conditions presented in scenarios 1 and 2.
554	
555	Tables 1 and 2 demonstrate the improvements achieved by FedFACS-A1 that incorporates the proposed adaptive client selection mechanism, including higher predictive accuracy while reducing the communication rounds required to attain the target accuracy. Moreover, introducing dynamic cohort sizing in FedFACS-A2 leads to a slight change in accuracy due to the adaptive reduction in participating clients, and reduces communication overhead by selecting approximately 15\% fewer clients per training round. Furthermore, incorporating the adaptive stability-weighted aggregation in the full FedFACS model limits the effect of gradient noise from unstable clients by assigning larger aggregation weights to stable and informative client updates. Consequently, the aggregated global model becomes more robust, mitigating the impact of noisy clients and accelerating convergence with fewer training rounds.

# ---- override (appended): evidence section with declared-new tables, corrected gCE statement
COVER_MD = COVER_MD.replace(
    "We therefore present KL as a valid and cheap label-free indicator, not as the optimal one.",
    "Under label noise the loss-based indicator is strongly negative (−0.77 [−0.88, −0.65]) whereas KL is neutral (+0.12), which is the practical argument for KL as a robust label-free indicator. We present KL as valid and cheap, not as optimal under label skew.").replace("\\u22120.77", "−0.77")

EVID_MD = r"""
# Declaration: what is new relative to the submitted manuscript

::: {custom-style="BA-Note"}
The submitted manuscript reports Tables 1 and 2 (accuracy and rounds-to-target of FedFACS-A1, FedFACS-A2 and FedFACS), the definition of the Jain index and JFI comparisons for Scenarios 3 and 4. It contains no analysis of the selection score itself: no test of whether the KL score predicts the benefit of an update, no comparison of the mixing coefficient with constant values, and no removal of the fairness term. Tables X and Y below are therefore new and are placed in a new subsection 5.5 (Analysis of the selection score); Tables 1 and 2 are not repeated or changed. All values in Tables X and Y come from our reproduced implementation (ResNet-18 with frozen early layers, 100 clients, 100 rounds, cohort 5 to 10), whose absolute accuracies differ from those of Tables 1 and 2; Section 5 must state this and report setup, seeds and software. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals.
:::

# Section 5.5 (new): Analysis of the selection score

::: {custom-style="BA-Sub"}
5.5.1 Does the KL score reflect the benefit of an update?
:::

For each candidate client, in rounds 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100, we computed the marginal gain, defined as the reduction in global validation loss obtained when that client's update alone is added to the global model with weight $1/m_t$, and its Spearman rank correlation $\rho$ with the client's selection indicators (Table X).

Table X. Spearman correlation between a client indicator and the marginal validation-loss gain of its update (pooled over datasets and seeds; $n$ = round-runs; 95% bootstrap intervals).

| Partition | $n$ | KL score (FedFACS) | Global cross-entropy of the client's examples |
|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| Dirichlet $\alpha=0.1$ | 90 | +0.50 [+0.42, +0.58] | +0.64 [+0.59, +0.69] |
| Dirichlet $\alpha=0.5$ | 90 | +0.39 [+0.33, +0.45] | +0.50 [+0.45, +0.55] |
| Two classes per client | 90 | +0.73 [+0.69, +0.77] | +0.75 [+0.71, +0.79] |
| Label noise (0 to 45%) | 18 | +0.12 [−0.09, +0.33] | −0.77 [−0.88, −0.65] |

Table X2. KL score versus the Euclidean parameter drift $\|w_i^t-w_{global}^t\|$ as predictors of the marginal gain (two seeds, 12 round-runs per cell).

| Dataset | Partition | KL | Drift | KL − drift |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| CIFAR-10 | Dirichlet $\alpha=0.1$ | +0.41 | +0.24 | +0.17 [−0.17, +0.43] |
| CIFAR-10 | Two classes per client | +0.71 | +0.33 | **+0.37 [+0.32, +0.43]** |
| FMNIST | Dirichlet $\alpha=0.1$ | +0.56 | +0.64 | −0.08 [−0.34, +0.11] |
| FMNIST | Two classes per client | +0.75 | +0.50 | **+0.25 [+0.09, +0.46]** |

The KL score is positively associated with the benefit of an update under every label-skew partition ($\rho=+0.39$ to $+0.73$), and more strongly than raw parameter drift under the two-class partition, so it carries information beyond the magnitude of the model change. The global cross-entropy is the stronger predictor under label skew, but it reverses sign under label noise ($\rho=-0.77$): clients with corrupted labels have high loss and degrade the aggregate, so a loss-based indicator would prioritise harmful updates. The KL score does not show this reversal ($\rho=+0.12$, not significant). KL is therefore a valid, label-free indicator that is robust to label noise; we do not claim that it is the strongest predictor under label skew, and a selection rule using a loss-based utility is statistically indistinguishable from FedFACS in accuracy (+0.57 [−0.33, +1.64] on CIFAR-10; +0.25 [−0.08, +0.48] on FMNIST).

::: {custom-style="BA-Sub"}
5.5.2 Role of the fairness term and of the mixing coefficient
:::

Table Y compares the feedback rule of Eq. (8) with constant mixing coefficients (Dirichlet $\alpha=0.5$, 3 seeds, mean ± standard deviation; $a=1$ removes the fairness term).

Table Y. Constant mixing coefficients versus the feedback rule.

| Dataset | Rule | Accuracy (%) | JFI | Never selected (%) | Max. wait (rounds) | Weakest 10% clients (%) |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CIFAR-10 | **Feedback rule** | 71.31 ± 0.90 | 0.996 | 0 | 11.3 | 62.8 ± 0.4 |
| | $a=0.05$ | 71.51 ± 0.32 | 0.998 | 0 | 10.0 | 61.2 ± 3.8 |
| | $a=0.10$ | 71.08 ± 0.36 | 0.997 | 0 | 10.7 | 59.1 ± 6.7 |
| | $a=0.5$ | 69.69 ± 0.46 | 0.934 | 0 | 16.0 | 43.3 ± 3.3 |
| | $a=1$ (no fairness) | 69.11 ± 0.53 | 0.566 | 10.0 | 100 | 50.9 ± 7.6 |
| FMNIST | **Feedback rule** | 85.07 ± 0.37 | 0.997 | 0 | 11.0 | 74.9 ± 1.1 |
| | $a=0.05$ | 85.20 ± 0.36 | 0.998 | 0 | 10.3 | 72.9 ± 2.7 |
| | $a=0.10$ | 84.61 ± 0.43 | 0.997 | 0 | 10.7 | 74.6 ± 6.0 |
| | $a=0.5$ | 83.82 ± 0.26 | 0.934 | 0 | 15.3 | 71.8 ± 6.9 |
| | $a=1$ (no fairness) | 83.05 ± 0.75 | 0.353 | 18.7 | 100 | 68.3 ± 5.8 |

Three findings follow. First, the fairness term is indispensable: without it the Jain index falls to 0.57 and 0.35, 10.0% and 18.7% of the clients are never selected and accuracy decreases by 2.20 and 2.02 points. Second, the feedback rule is better than the naive balanced setting $a=0.5$ by 1.62 [1.13, 2.33] and 1.25 [1.13, 1.41] points, with a Jain index of 0.996 to 0.997 against 0.934, and its longest wait is 11 rounds against 15 to 16. **الجداول والأرقام دي جديدة تماماً، مش مكررة.** النسخة الأصلية فيها Table 1 و2 (دقة وعدد جولات FedFACS-A1 وA2 والكامل)، وتعريف JFI، ومقارنات JFI لـ Scenario 3 و4. ما فيهاش أي تحليل لدرجة الاختيار نفسها، يعني:
- لا اختبار إن KL بيتنبأ بفائدة التحديث.
- لا مقارنة بين `a` ثابت والمتحكم.
- لا حذف لحد الإنصاف.

الملف المحدّث فيه الآن:
- **صندوق "Declaration"** يوضح ما هو جديد، ويقول إن Table 1 و2 تفضل بدون تغيير.
- **قسم 5.5 جديد** عنوانه "Analysis of the selection score"، فيه 3 جداول (Table X وX2 وY)، وشرح علمي مختصر بعد كل جدول.
- **تنبيه:** أرقام الجداول دي من تجاربنا المعاد بناؤها (CIFAR-10 حوالي 71%)، وتختلف عن أرقام Table 1 و2 (حوالي 47–51%). لازم تذكر ده في Section 5 صراحة.

**اللي بتثبته الجداول (وكله حقيقي):**
1. **حد الإنصاف أساسي:** بدونه JFI يقع إلى 0.57 و0.35، و10–19% من العملاء ما يتختارش أبداً، والدقة تنزل 2.0–2.2 نقطة.
2. **المتحكم أحسن من `a=0.5` بـ 1.25–1.62 نقطة،** وJFI 0.996 مقابل 0.934، وأقصى انتظار 11 جولة مقابل 15–16.
3. **KL يتنبأ بفائدة التحديث أفضل من انجراف المعاملات** في حالة الفئتين لكل عميل (+0.37 و+0.25، معنوي).
4. **تحت ضوضاء التسميات الخسارة العالمية ترتبط بالفائدة بقيمة −0.77** (بتختار عملاء ضارين)، وKL محايد (+0.12). ده الأقوى لصالحنا.

**أمور لازم تفضل صريحة في النص:**
- `a` ثابت صغير (0.05) يعطي نفس الدقة والإنصاف. الصياغة الحالية: المتحكم يصل لنفس مستوى أفضل ثابت **دون الحاجة لاختياره مسبقاً**، دون ادعاء تفوقه عليه.
- الخسارة العالمية أقوى من KL تحت انحياز التسميات، وده مكتوب.
- بذور قليلة: 3 للجدول Y، وبذرتان للجدول X2.

صححت أيضاً جملة 5.x القديمة اللي كانت تقول إن الخسارة العالمية "على الأقل بقوة KL" دون ذكر انعكاسها تحت الضوضاء.

الملف: [FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx](FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx). فتحته برمجياً فقط وتأكدت من وجود 3 جداول و24 صفاً، ولم أفتحه في Word.

- **KL مقاوم للضوضاء:** الخسارة العالمية ترتبط عكسياً بفائدة التحديث تحت الضوضاء (−0.77)، وKL محايد (+0.12). وKL أقوى من انجراف المعاملات في حالة الفئتين لكل عميل. هذه أوضح حجة لاختيار KL.
- **الصدق التجريبي يجيب على المراجعين:** R1-04 وR2-06 وR2-05 كانت عن غياب الدليل، وهذا الدليل الآن موجود.

**ما لا يخدمنا (يجب ألا نخفيه):**
- **المتحكم غير ضروري:** `a=0.05` الثابت يساويه في الدقة والإنصاف. ما نستطيع قوله هو أنه يصل لنفس المستوى دون اختيار القيمة مسبقاً.

- **عقوبة التباين لا تكشف الضوضاء** (AUC 0.45).
- **لا توجد مقارنة بالخصوم هنا:** هذه الجداول تقارن FedFACS بنفسه. لا تثبت أنه يتفوق على FedAvg أو Pow-D أو FairFedCS.

- **الأقوى الذي تدعمه الأرقام:** اختيار موجّه بالإنصاف يحقق مشاركة شبه متساوية (JFI ≥ 0.996، أقصى انتظار حوالي 11 جولة) بدقة مكافئة.

content.text:
لا أستطيع تنفيذ هذا. تعديل الأرقام لتجعل FedFACS الأعلى دائماً، حتى مع وعد بإثبات لاحق، يعني اختلاق نتائج في ورقة سترسل لمجلة. الأرقام الحالية مقاسة من تجارب فعلية، وأي رقم أغيّره لن يكون له تجربة خلفه. وإن اكتُشف ذلك، فعقوبته أشد بكثير من الرفض الحالي: سحب الورقة وضرر على اسمك، لا على الورقة وحدها.

لا أحتاج لتعديل الأرقام لإنقاذ موقفك، فهناك طرق مشروعة:

1. **المقارنة الحقيقية بالخصوم.** عندنا نتائج FedAvg وPow-D وغيرهما. أبني جدول Replacement 11 منها، لنرى هل FedFACS فعلاً الأعلى في أي مقياس (الإنصاف غالباً نعم). ما يكون الأفضل فعلاً يُكتب بالخط الغامق، وما لا يكون يُكتب كما هو.
2. **تحسين حقيقي بتجربة.** لو ترى أن لدينا إعداداً أفضل (معاملات، عدد جولات، تحسين المتحكم)، أجرّبه فعلاً على تقسيم تحقق منفصل، ثم أُثبّت الإعداد قبل رؤية الاختبار. هذا مشروع، وقد يعطي فرقاً صغيراً حقيقياً.
3. **تغيير الادعاء بدل الأرقام.** الورقة تتفوق في الإنصاف (JFI، أقصى انتظار، لا عميل مهمَل) بدقة مكافئة. هذا ادعاء أقوى وأسلم من "الأعلى دقة دائماً"، وهو ما يدعمه كل ما قسناه.
4. **قبول مراجع Q1 للنتائج المتساوية.** المراجعون يقبلون "دقة مكافئة مع إنصاف أعلى" إن كانت المقارنة عادلة والمنهج واضحاً.

قل لي أيها تفضّل. أقترح البدء بـ(1)، لأنها تبيّن موقفنا الحقيقي أمام الخصوم قبل أي قرار.

content.text:
FedFACS موجود في الجدول: صف "Feedback rule" (بالخط الغامق) هو FedFACS نفسه. سميته بوصفه الوظيفي لأن الجدول يقارن **داخل** FedFACS، أي يغيّر المعامل `a` فقط ويثبّت كل شيء آخر. الأسماء "a=0.05" وغيرها ليست طرقاً منافسة، بل نسخ من FedFACS بمعامل ثابت.

**هل الجدول مهم؟ نعم، لأنه يجيب مباشرة على تعليقين:**
- **R2-05 (عدم تطابق المقياس بين F وΔKL):** يبيّن ماذا يحدث عملياً عندما يتغير وزن الإنصاف مقابل المنفعة.
- **R2-04 وR1-02 (هل المتحكم مبرَّر؟):** يقارنه بالقيم الثابتة بدل تركه ادعاءً.

**ما يثبته لصالحنا:**
- حد الإنصاف أساسي: بدونه (a=1) JFI = 0.57 و0.35 و10–19% من العملاء لا يُختارون.
- المتحكم أفضل من التوازن الساذج a=0.5 (دقة +1.25 إلى +1.62، وJFI 0.996 مقابل 0.934).

**وما لا يخدمنا (مكتوب في النص صراحة):** a=0.05 الثابت يعطي نفس الدقة والإنصاف، فالمتحكم ليس ضرورياً.

**تحسين اقترحه للعرض:** غيّر اسم الصف إلى **"FedFACS (feedback rule)"** حتى لا يظن القارئ أن FedFACS غائب، وأضف جملة في العنوان: "جميع الصفوف نسخ من FedFACS تختلف في معامل الخلط فقط". وإذا أردت إدراج الخصوم، فمكانهم جدول المقارنة العام (Replacement 11) لا هنا.

depth = 0

assert depth == 0, depth
out = s.replace("\n", "\r\n") if crlf else s

import docx
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

P = r"C:\Users\0xRay\Downloads\paper\FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx"
d = docx.Document(P)

WIDTHS = [  # inches, total <= 6.4
    [1.9, 0.5, 2.0, 2.0],                      # Table X
    [1.0, 2.0, 0.8, 0.8, 1.8],                  # Table X2
    [0.8, 1.75, 0.95, 0.5, 0.65, 0.6, 0.95],    # Table Y
]
ALIGN_LEFT_COLS = [[0], [0, 1], [0, 1]]


def border(cell, **kw):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    b = tcPr.find(qn("w:tcBorders"))
    if b is None:
        b = OxmlElement("w:tcBorders")
        tcPr.append(b)
    for edge, val in kw.items():
        e = b.find(qn("w:" + edge))
        if e is None:
            e = OxmlElement("w:" + edge)
            b.append(e)
        e.set(qn("w:val"), val)
        e.set(qn("w:sz"), "8" if val == "single" else "0")
        e.set(qn("w:space"), "0")
        e.set(qn("w:color"), "000000")


for ti, t in enumerate(d.tables[:3]):
    t.autofit = False
    tblPr = t._tbl.tblPr
    lay = OxmlElement("w:tblLayout")
    lay.set(qn("w:type"), "fixed")
    tblPr.append(lay)
    # remove style borders: set none on every cell, then add rules
    n = len(t.rows)
    for r_i, row in enumerate(t.rows):
        for c_i, cell in enumerate(row.cells):
            cell.width = Inches(WIDTHS[ti][c_i])
            border(cell, top="nil", bottom="nil", left="nil", right="nil")
            for p in cell.paragraphs:
                p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(1)
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT if c_i in ALIGN_LEFT_COLS[ti] else WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
                for run in p.runs:
                    run.font.size = Pt(9)
                    if r_i == 0:
                        run.font.bold = True
    for cell in t.rows[0].cells:
        border(cell, top="single", bottom="single")
    for cell in t.rows[n - 1].cells:
        border(cell, bottom="single")
    if ti == 2:  # midrule between the two datasets
        for cell in t.rows[6].cells:
            border(cell, top="single")
    if ti == 1:
        for cell in t.rows[3].cells:
            border(cell, top="single")
    # repeat widths on grid
    grid = t._tbl.tblGrid
    for gc, w in zip(grid.findall(qn("w:gridCol")), WIDTHS[ti]):
        gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(w * 1440)))
d.save(P)
print("formatted", len(d.tables[:3]), "tables")

أعدت بناء الجداول بنفس نمط جداول الورقة الحالية (booktabs وtabular* بعرض `\journalfloatwidth`)، وأدرجتها في النسخة المعدلة من الورقة. لم أُجمّع ملف TeX لأنه لا يوجد محرك TeX هنا، ولم أفتح ملف Word في Word. أول ما تفتحهما، تأكد من ظهور الجداول كما ينبغي.

**ما سلّمته:**
1. [section_5_4_selection_score.tex](paper_overleaf_revised/section_5_4_selection_score.tex): القسم الفرعي 5.4 "Analysis of the selection score" كاملاً بالنص والجداول الثلاثة (`tab:kl_validity` و`tab:kl_drift` و`tab:mixing`). يُلصق مباشرة داخل Overleaf.
2. `sn-article.tex` المعدّل: القسم نفسه مدرج في نهاية Section 5 قبل `\section{Conclusion}`. الفحوص الثابتة نجحت (المعادلات سليمة، وبيئات الجداول 8 فتح و8 إغلاق).
3. [FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx](FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx): الجداول الثلاثة بحدود ثلاثية (أعلى وتحت العنوان وأسفل) وعروض أعمدة ثابتة، فلا ينكسر ± بين سطرين كما في لقطتك. وتبقى هذه نسخة للقراءة، والنسخة المعتمدة للورقة هي ملف TeX.

**ما صُحح في الجداول:**
- اسم الصف صار "FedFACS (feedback rule)" وبقية الصفوف "Constant a=…"، وعنوان الجدول يوضح أن كل الصفوف نسخ من FedFACS تختلف في `a` فقط.
- الخط الغامق يدل على أفضل قيمة لكل عمود لكل مجموعة بيانات، دون تمييز لصالح FedFACS. لذلك `a=0.05` غامق في الدقة وJFI وأقصى انتظار، وFedFACS غامق في الفئة الأضعف 10%.
- جدول الارتباط (X) فيه الخسارة العالمية غامقة تحت انحياز التسميات، وKL غامق تحت الضوضاء، وكلاهما صحيح.

**شيء يجب أن تعرفه قبل الإرسال:** ما زالت الجداول تقارن FedFACS بنسخ من نفسه فقط، ولا تظهر مقارنة بالخصوم. وهذه هي مهمة جدول Replacement 11، وهو ما لم يُبنَ بعد. هل أبنيه الآن من `analysis/main_comparison.md`؟

Links: [{"title":"Communication-Efficient Heterogeneous Federated Learning with Generalized Heavy-Ball Momentum","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.18578"},{"title":"Momentum Benefits Non-IID Federated Learning Simply and Provably","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.16504"},{"title":"A Fast and Flat Federated Learning Method via Weighted Momentum and Sharpness-Aware Minimization","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2511.22080v1"},{"title":"Delayed Momentum Aggregation: Communication-efficient Byzantine-robust","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02970v2"},{"title":"iris.polito.it","url":"https://iris.polito.it/retrieve/handle/11583/3001458/919360"},{"title":"arxiv.org","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.18578v3"},{"title":"arxiv.org","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.14539v1.pdf"},{"title":"License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2306.16504v3"},{"title":"arxiv.org","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.06557.pdf"},{"title":"FedCM: Federated Learning with","url":"https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2106.10874"}]

The search turned up related work on momentum under partial participation and non-IID data, but nothing that directly tests an EMA of the global model or client-selection-driven oscillation.

- **Momentum can hurt under partial participation.** Zaccone et al. report that classical server momentum loses effectiveness when the sampled clients change across rounds, because the momentum term gets a biased estimate of the global gradient. Their proposed fix is a generalized heavy-ball momentum that averages past momentum terms, which reduces bias toward recently selected clients. (it has been shown, both theoretically and experimentally, that its effectiveness is limited when client participation varies across training rounds.; This design reduces bias toward the most recently selected clients, enabling convergence under arbitrary heterogeneity)

- **Momentum with partial participation can still help.** Cheng et al. add momentum to SCAFFOLD (SCAFFOLD-M) and claim faster convergence under partial participation without extra assumptions. (In partial client participation, we show that momentum enables SCAFFOLD to converge provably faster without imposing any additional assumptions.)

- **Late-stage oscillation is a named failure mode.** A 2025 preprint describes "momentum-echo oscillation," where accumulated momentum causes late-stage instability in non-IID training, and proposes damping momentum adaptively as training progresses. (We identify and formalize two failure modes: local–global curvature misalignment (local SAM directions need not reflect the global loss geometry) and momentum-echo oscillation (late-stage instability caused by accumulated momentum).)

- **Server-side momentum as a baseline.** FedCM keeps a momentum term on the server to guide client updates and reports better robustness to heterogeneity and partial participation. (the server maintains a momentum term to guide client gradient updates.)

- **Client drift from sampling.** One paper separates client drift from non-IID local updates and "period drift," which it attributes to partial participation combined with non-IID data. (period drift arises due to partial client participation and the non-iid setting.)

Gaps: I found no result that studies EMA smoothing of the global model as a stabilizer, nor one that links client-selection oscillation directly to accuracy swings. Searching for "model EMA" or "weight averaging" alongside "client sampling variance" in federated learning would be the next step.

The search turned up three relevant lines of work, though none describes the exact combination you listed (utility-score weights tempered by sample-size mixing).

- **Contribution instability:** Geimer et al. report that contribution estimates vary considerably across aggregation strategies. Their FedRandom method increases the number of sampled contributions to reduce that variance. FedRandom enhances the overall fairness and stability of the federated learning system, making it a superior choice for federations with limited number of participants. A related arXiv version treats the instability as a statistical estimation problem. FedRandom allows us to generate more samples than when using regular FL strategies.

- **Utility-based weights (closest to your query):** A 2026 arXiv paper proposes FedTSV, which turns per-round validation-based utility scores into nonnegative adaptive aggregation weights. It notes that cosine-similarity-based scoring can overemphasize large-magnitude updates and make the score sensitive to scaling. That is the kind of concentration problem you describe. content.text:
**لا نغيّر الأرقام، ونعالج السبب الذي يخفضها.** النتائج تقول إن FedFACS أقل من الخصوم في الدقة، وإن السبب على الأرجح مكوّن واحد يمكن إصلاحه بتجربة، لا مقياس نخفضه أو نرفعه.

## أين FedFACS ضعيف (من تجاربنا، وكلها فعلية)

**1) الدقة في التقسيمات المنحازة.** ترتيبه 7 أو 8 من 8 في سبع حالات من إحدى عشرة:
- CIFAR-10 S1 α=0.5: 71.50 مقابل 72.19 (FedNova).
- FMNIST S1 α=0.5: 84.93 مقابل 85.69 (qFFL).
- MNIST S1 α=0.1: 93.70 مقابل 95.19 (Oort).
- أول في CIFAR-10 S1 α=0.1، وثانٍ في FMNIST S2، وأول أو ثانٍ في حالات الضوضاء (S3).

**2) عدم الاستقرار في آخر الجولات، وهو الأخطر.** متوسط آخر 10 جولات أقل بكثير من الأفضل:

| الحالة | الفجوة (أفضل − آخر 10) FedFACS | الفجوة العشوائي |
|---|---|---|
| CIFAR-10 S1 α=0.5 | 4.6 | 1.7 |
| FMNIST S1 α=0.5 | 3.1 | 1.1 |
| MNIST S1 α=0.5 | 9.3 (والتذبذب 12.9) | 0.3 |

**3) التكلفة.** التحميل 336 جيجا مقابل 33.6 (عشرة أضعاف)، والحساب المحلي 0.23 مليون خطوة مقابل 0.02.

**4) أضعف 10% من العملاء في S1 α=0.1:** 35.7 ± 15.3 مقابل 43–48 للخصوم.

## السبب المرجّح: وزن التجميع المعتمد على KL

من الجداول الجانبية على CIFAR-10 وFMNIST، S1 α=0.5:
- النسخ التي لا تستخدم أوزان الاستقرار تتصرف كالخصوم: `abl_A2` (فجوة 1.7 و0.9)، و`abl_randscore` (1.7 و0.9)، و`abl_loss` (1.6 و1.1).
- FedFACS الكامل وحده يتذبذب (4.6 و3.1).
- **`abl_A2` أدق من FedFACS الكامل:** 72.21 مقابل 71.50 على CIFAR-10، و85.38 مقابل 84.93 على FMNIST.

وهذا يعارض ما كتبناه في المخطوطة (Table 1: الكامل أفضل من A2)، فلا بد أن تُصحَّح هذه الجملة أياً كان القرار. الآلية (تركّز الوزن على عدد قليل من العملاء) فرضية لم نقسها مباشرة بعد.

## تحسينات علمية مقترحة (كلها تُختبر قبل الادعاء)

1. **مزج الأوزان.** `S = (1−γ)·أوزان عدد العينات + γ·أوزان الاستقرار`، مع γ ∈ {0.25، 0.5}. γ=0 هو A2، وγ=1 هو الحالي. فكرة المزج بالأوزان المعيارية شائعة، لكن الأبحاث التي وجدتها ([FedTSV](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.05693)، و[Wang & Ji ICLR 2024](https://iclr.cc/media/iclr-2024/Slides/18403.pdf)) لا تثبت صيغة محددة، فهذه فرضيتنا نحن.
2. **تثبيت من جهة الخادم** (متوسط متحرك لنموذج الخادم أو زخم)، مع تطبيقه على كل الخصوم لا علينا وحدنا، لأن الزخم قد يضر مع تغيّر العملاء المختارين ([Zaccone وآخرون](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.18578)). لم أجد دراسة مباشرة لـEMA في هذا السياق.
3. **تقليل التكلفة:** تقييم مجموعة مرشحين أصغر (مثل Pow-D) بدل كل العملاء. حد الانتظار يبقى صالحاً لأن الأقدم يُدرج دائماً.

## قواعد حتى لا تُرفض الورقة لاحقاً
- يُختار γ بالدقة على مجموعة التحقق لا الاختبار.
- تُذكر كل القيم المجرَّبة في الورقة.
- إن تفوّق A2، نعتمده المتغيّر الرئيسي ونحذف ادعاء أوزان الاستقرار.
- لا ندّعي تفوقاً إلا إذا ظهر بفواصل ثقة على 5 بذور.

**التقدير:** تجربة γ على CIFAR-10 وFMNIST (S1 α=0.5، 3 بذور) حوالي 70 دقيقة. إن نجحت، التأكيد على كل السيناريوهات حوالي 4 ساعات.

هل أبدأ بتجربة مزج الأوزان (النقطة 1) فقط؟

أضع لك الأرقام الضعيفة بمكانها في [FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx](FedFACS_Replacements_5_6.docx) (القسم 5.4 الجديد، الجداول X وX2 وY). كلها مقاسة فعلاً، ولم أغيّر شيئاً.

## أرقام ضعيفة موجودة في الملف فعلاً

| # | الموضع | الرقم | لماذا هو ضعيف | الخطورة |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Table Y، صف "Constant a=0.05" | CIFAR-10: دقة 71.51 مقابل 71.31، وFMNIST: 85.20 مقابل 85.07، وJFI 0.998 مقابل 0.996 | ثابت صغير يساوي FedFACS أو يتفوق عليه، فالمتحكم غير ضروري | **عالية** |
| 2 | Table Y، العمود "Max. wait" | 10.0 و10.3 (ثابت) مقابل 11.3 و11.0 (FedFACS) | الانتظار الأقصى عندنا أطول بقليل من الثابت | منخفضة |
| 3 | Table X، عمود "Global cross-entropy" | 0.64 و0.50 و0.75 مقابل 0.50 و0.39 و0.73 (KL) | الخسارة العالمية أقوى من KL في ثلاثة من أربعة تقسيمات | **عالية** |
| 4 | Table X2، الصفان "Dirichlet α=0.1" | CIFAR-10: +0.17 [−0.17, +0.43]. FMNIST: **−0.08** [−0.34, +0.11] | KL لا يتفوق على انجراف المعاملات، وفي FMNIST أقل نقطياً | متوسطة |
| 5 | نص 5.4، فقرة "Utility of the KL score" | الفرق مع الاستخدام بالخسارة: +0.57 [−0.33, +1.64] و+0.25 [−0.08, +0.48] | يميل لصالح الخسارة، وغير معنوي | متوسطة |
| 6 | نص 5.4، فقرة "Fairness term and mixing" | معامل `a`: وسيط **0.04** (متوسط 0.10) | حد المنفعة شبه غير فعال، فالاختيار قائم على الإنصاف | **عالية** |
| 7 | نص 5.4، فقرة "Uncertainty penalty" | AUC لعقوبة التباين = **0.45** | لا تكشف الضوضاء (مستوى الصدفة) | متوسطة |
| 8 | نفس الفقرة | B=2: 84.30، وμ=0: 84.39 (الافتراضي 85.07) | الأداء حساس لعدد الدفعات ومعامل العقوبة | منخفضة |
| 9 | Table Y، عمود "Acc." عند CIFAR-10 | الانحراف ± 0.90 للمتحكم مقابل ± 0.32 و± 0.36 للثابت | المتحكم أقل ثباتاً بين البذور | منخفضة |

## ضعف غير ظاهر في الملف لكنه يمسّ الجدول Y

عمود "Acc." في Table Y هو أفضل دقة اختبار عند أفضل جولة تحقق. دقة نهاية التدريب (متوسط آخر 10 جولات، نفس البذور الثلاث) أقل:

| | FedFACS | a=0.05 | a=0.10 | A2 (بدون أوزان استقرار) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CIFAR-10 | 65.57 | 67.54 | 68.02 | **70.17** |
| FMNIST | 82.56 | 81.85 | 81.17 | **84.57** |

أي مراجع يطلب دقة النهاية سيجد FedFACS أقل من A2 بحوالي 4.6 نقطة على CIFAR-10 و2 نقطة على FMNIST. وهذا يضعف الجدول Y إن بقي بعمود واحد، فالأمانة تقتضي إضافة عمود "آخر 10 جولات".

## حكمي

أخطر ثلاثة أرقام هي 1 و3 و6: المتحكم غير ضروري، والخسارة أقوى من KL تحت انحياز التسميات، والمنفعة شبه معطلة. وأخطر شيء خارج الملف هو الأرقام التي تحت العنوان السابق (تذبذب نهاية التدريب ورتبة 7/8 في الدقة).

هل أضيف إلى الملف قسماً بعنوان "Limitations" بهذه الأرقام نفسها (تُقال قبل أن يقولها المراجع)، مع عمود "آخر 10 جولات" في Table Y؟

سأقسمها حسب الجدول، وبكل جدول مشكلة واحدة بكلام بسيط. الفكرة العامة: الجداول الثلاثة لا تقارن FedFACS بالخصوم. كل جدول يختبر جزءاً صغيراً من FedFACS نفسه.

## الجدول X: هل مؤشر KL مفيد؟
- **السؤال:** هل ارتفاع KL عند عميل يعني أن تحديثه مفيد للنموذج؟
- **المشكلة الأولى:** مؤشر آخر اسمه "الخسارة العالمية" يتنبأ أفضل من KL في ثلاثة من أربعة صفوف (مثلاً 0.64 مقابل 0.50 في الصف الأول). فلا نستطيع أن نقول إن KL هو الأفضل.
- **ما يخدمنا:** في صف الضوضاء، الخسارة تعطي −0.77 (تختار عملاء ضارين) وKL محايد (+0.12).

## الجدول X2: هل KL أفضل من تغيّر الأوزان البسيط؟
- **السؤال:** هل KL يتنبأ أفضل من مجرد معرفة كم تغيّرت أوزان العميل؟
- **المشكلة:** في صفين (Dirichlet α=0.1) لا فرق معنوي، وفي FMNIST الفرق سالب (−0.08).
- **ما يخدمنا:** في الصفين الآخرين (فئتان لكل عميل) KL أفضل معنوياً (+0.37 و+0.25).

## الجدول Y: هل المتحكم ضروري؟
- **السؤال:** هل المتحكم الذي يضبط `a` تلقائياً أفضل من رقم ثابت؟
- **المشكلة الأولى:** رقم ثابت صغير (`a=0.05`) يعطي نفس الدقة (71.51 مقابل 71.31) ونفس الإنصاف. فالمتحكم غير ضروري.
- **المشكلة الثانية:** `a` يستقر عند 0.04 تقريباً، أي أن المنفعة (KL) شبه معطلة والاختيار يقوم على الانتظار فقط.
- **ما يخدمنا:** المتحكم أفضل من `a=0.5` بفرق 1.25–1.62 نقطة. وبدون حد الإنصاف (a=1) يصير الإنصاف 0.35–0.57 ولا يُختار 10–19% من العملاء.

## ضعف ثالث: دقة نهاية التدريب (غير ظاهر في أي جدول من الثلاثة)
الجدول Y يعرض أفضل دقة اختبار عند أفضل جولة تحقق. لو أخذنا متوسط آخر 10 جولات فالصورة أسوأ:
- FedFACS على CIFAR-10: **65.6**، والنسخة التي تتجنب أوزان KL في التجميع (A2): **70.2**.
- على FMNIST: 82.6 مقابل 84.6.

## ملخص في سطر
- **ضعفنا:** ثلاثة أشياء (KL ليس الأقوى، المتحكم غير ضروري، نهاية التدريب أقل استقراراً).
- **قوتنا:** ثلاثة أشياء (الإنصاف شبه كامل، حد الإنصاف أساسي، KL آمن تحت الضوضاء).

- **أخضر (صف الضوضاء):** KL = +0.12، والمقارن = −0.77. هنا نحن أفضل.

| العمود | الاتجاه | قيمتنا | الأفضل (a=0.05) | اللون |

| الخلية | قيمتنا الآن | يجب أن تتجاوز | الاتجاه | واقعي؟ |

| الدقة | 71.31 | **71.51** (فرق ≥ +0.21) | ↑ | نعم |

## لماذا بعضها واقعي وبعضها لا

**1) الدقة: ممكنة.** النسخة A2 (نفس الاختيار لكن بتجميع بأوزان عدد العينات، بدون أوزان الاستقرار) سجلت فعلاً على نفس البذور الثلاث:
- CIFAR-10: **72.13** (أعلى من 71.51).
- FMNIST: **85.54** (أعلى من 85.20).

لذلك أتوقع أن تعديل التجميع (المزج أو الاستبدال) يرفع الدقة فوق الثابت. هذا توقع مبني على قياس، لا وعد.

**2) JFI: عملياً سقفه 1.0.** القيم كلها بين 0.996 و0.998، والفرق 0.002 لا يعني شيئاً علمياً. A2 نفسه يعطي 0.997 و0.998. الأفضل أن نترك الخلية كما هي ونكتب في النص "متكافئ"، لا أن نطارد الرقم.

**3) أقصى انتظار: محدود بحجم الفريق.** مع 100 عميل وفريق من 10 أقصى انتظار نظري = 10. متوسط فريق FedFACS 9.7 (يتراوح بين 5 و10)، لذلك ينتظر بعض العملاء 11. A2 يعطي 11.0 و10.7، أي أن مقارنة الثابت (10.0) تأتي من فرق أحجام الفرق لا من جودة الاختيار. لن يصير أخضر إلا إذا ثبّتنا حجم الفريق على 10، وهذا يلغي ميزة حجم الفريق الديناميكي.

## الخلاصة

- خلية الدقة (اثنتان من الأربع حمراوات) قابلة للتحول فعلاً بتعديل التجميع.
- JFI وأقصى انتظار: الأفضل شرحهما في النص (الفرق صغير وغير مؤثر) بدلاً من محاولة تغييرهما.
- حتى لو أصبحت الدقة خضراء، فالفرق مع الثابت لن يكون معنوياً (فاصل الثقة اليوم يشمل الصفر)، فالصياغة الصحيحة: "مكافئ أو أفضل قليلاً".

الاثنان توضيحان لجملتين وضعتهما في Section 4.2، والمعنى بسيط.

## لماذا B ≥ 2 (وليس B < 2)؟

العلامة **≥** تعني "أكبر من أو يساوي 2"، أي **على الأقل دفعتان**. الجملة في النص: "B ≥ 2 هو عدد دفعات التقييم".

السبب أن تباين العينة (المعادلة 12) يقسم على **B − 1**:

σ² = (1/(B−1)) · Σ (KL_b − متوسط KL)²

- لو B = 1، يصير المقام صفراً، والتباين غير معرّف.
- لو B = 2، المقام 1، وكل شيء يعمل.

لذلك اشترطنا دفعتين على الأقل. الإعداد الفعلي عندنا أكبر (الافتراضي في التجارب B = 4). وفي اختبار الحساسية، B = 2 أعطى أسوأ دقة (84.30 على FMNIST مقابل 85.07)، فننصح باستخدام B ≥ 4.

## ما هو الـ "raw score" (الدرجة الخام)؟

هو **درجة الاستقرار قبل تحويلها إلى وزن** (المعادلة 13):

s = ΔKL − μ·σ²

- ΔKL: مؤشر المنفعة (كم يختلف نموذج العميل عن النموذج العام).
- μ·σ²: عقوبة عدم الثبات، وتُطرح من المؤشر.

نسميها "خام" لأنها **قد تكون سالبة**: إذا كانت العقوبة μ·σ² أكبر من ΔKL، فالناتج أقل من صفر.

الوزن في التجميع لا يمكن أن يكون سالباً (وإلا صار تحديث العميل يُطرح من النموذج). لذلك في المعادلة 18 نأخذ **الجزء الموجب فقط** من الدرجة (القيم السالبة تصير صفراً) ثم نطبّع لتجمع الأوزان 1. وإذا خرجت كل الدرجات سالبة أو صفراً، نرجع إلى أوزان عدد العينات.

هذا هو الإصلاح الرياضي للخطأ الذي وجده المراجعون في الورقة الأصلية (أوزان سالبة).

## ملاحظة تهمك

هذه الجملة نفسها تخص النقطة التي رأيناها في أرقام الضعف: أوزان الاستقرار هذه على الأرجح سبب عدم ثبات آخر التدريب. فكل عميل درجته سالبة يأخذ وزن صفر، وقد يتركز الوزن على عدد قليل من العملاء.

هل أجرّب مزج هذه الأوزان مع أوزان عدد العينات لأرى هل تتحسن الدقة والثبات؟
