"""Builds FedFACS_Missing_Sections_5-8.docx: every new element of Replacements 5-8 that does not exist in the original paper,
with the proofs and a ledger that ties every number to the raw runs (tools/verify_claims.py)."""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import docx
import pypandoc
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt

import build_78 as N
import build_final56 as B

P, WORK, BS, BSR = B.P, B.WORK, B.BS, B.BSR
OUTF = os.path.join(P, "FedFACS_Missing_Sections_5-8.docx")
NL = chr(10)
CLAIMS = json.load(open(os.path.join(WORK, "claims.json"), encoding="utf8"))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- tables as markdown
XP, X2P, YP = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r"(?=Table X2\.|Table Y\.)", B.TABLES_MD.strip())]
ZP, WP = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r"(?=Table W\.)", N.TABLES_MD.strip())]
TABLE_MD = {"tab:kl_validity": XP, "tab:kl_drift": X2P, "tab:mixing": YP, "tab:cohort": ZP}

HEAD = r"""
::: {custom-style="BA-Title"}
FedFACS: the new sections, with their proofs and the evidence for every number (Replacements 5 to 8)
:::

::: {custom-style="BA-Note"}
Purpose. The original paper has no Section 4.3, no Section 5.4, no Tables X, X2, Y, Z, no Eqs. (5a), (5b), (12a) and no coefficient kappa in Eq. (18). Replacements 5 to 8 refer to them. This file contains all of them in one place: where each is inserted (part 1), the proofs of the statements that the new text makes (part 2), the full text of the two new sections with their tables (parts 3 and 4), the new equations (part 5), and a ledger that recomputes every number of the new text from the raw run files (part 6). Evidence comes from our reproduced runs (ResNet-18 with frozen early layers, 100 clients, 100 rounds, cohorts of 5 to 10 clients); the manuscript must state that its numbers come from this implementation.
:::

# 1. What is new and where it is inserted

| New element | Insert at | Used by | Reviewer comments |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Section 4.3 Properties of FedFACS (Propositions 1 to 3, waiting-time guard) | after Section 4.2, before Section 5 | Replacements 6, 7, 8 | R1-02, R1-10, R2-04, R2-18 |
| Section 5.4 Analysis of the selection score | end of Section 5, before the Conclusion | Replacements 5, 6, 7, 8 | R1-04, R1-05, R1-06, R1-10, R1-11, R1-18, R2-04, R2-05, R2-06, R2-07, R2-09 |
| Tables X, X2 (utility validity and drift), Y (mixing coefficient), Z (cohort rules) | inside Section 5.4 | Replacements 5, 6, 7 | as above |
| Eqs. (5a), (5b), (12a); Eq. (16) with the relative-pace option; Eq. (18) with kappa | Section 4.2 | Replacements 5, 7, 8 | R1-03, R1-04, R1-05, R1-06, R2-06, R2-07 |
| the aggregation family S = (1 - kappa) n_i / sum n_j + kappa q_i and its default kappa = 0 | Section 4.2, Eq. (18) | Replacement 8 | R1-03, R1-11, R2-07 |

Tables X, X2, Y and Z are numbered by LaTeX in the manuscript; the letters are used here only to name them.
"""

LEMMAS = r"""
# 2. Proofs of the statements made by the new text

**Lemma A (direction of the feedback, Eq. (8); R1-02, R2-04).** Let $g_i^t=\dfrac{\nu^t(\Delta KL_i^t-F_i^t)}{\lambda F_i^t+\lvert\nu^t(\Delta KL_i^t-F_i^t)\rvert}$, so that $a_i^t=\mathrm{clip}\big(\beta a_i^{t-1}+(1-\beta)g_i^t,0,1\big)$ with $a_i^{t-1}\in[0,1]$.

(i) $\lvert g_i^t\rvert<1$ and $\operatorname{sign} g_i^t=\operatorname{sign}\big(\nu^t(\Delta KL_i^t-F_i^t)\big)$, because $\lambda F_i^t\ge\lambda>0$.

(ii) If $\nu^t>0$ and $\Delta KL_i^t<F_i^t$, then $g_i^t<0$, hence $\beta a_i^{t-1}+(1-\beta)g_i^t<\beta a_i^{t-1}\le a_i^{t-1}$ and, since $a_i^{t-1}\ge 0$, the clip gives $a_i^t\le a_i^{t-1}$, with strict inequality unless $a_i^{t-1}=0$.

(iii) If $\nu^t>0$ and $\Delta KL_i^t>F_i^t$, then $g_i^t>0$ and $a_i^t>a_i^{t-1}$ if and only if $g_i^t>a_i^{t-1}$.

So a positive deviation signal lowers the utility weight exactly when the utility score is below the fairness term, and can raise it otherwise. In the reproduced runs the utility score was below $F_i^t$ in 82.7% of the client-rounds, and the mean coefficient decreased in 98.2% of the 4,316 rounds with $\nu^t>0$ (ledger K4, E1). $\square$

**Lemma B (cohort rule, Eq. (16); R1-06, R2-08, R2-09).** Let $m(e)=\min\{C_{k_{\max}},\max\{C_{k_{\min}},\lfloor C_{k_{\min}}+(C_{k_{\max}}-C_{k_{\min}})(1-\mathrm{clip}(e,0,1))+\tfrac12\rfloor\}\}$.

(i) $m(e)$ is an integer with $C_{k_{\min}}\le m(e)\le C_{k_{\max}}$ for every real $e$, because of the clamp.

(ii) $m$ is nonincreasing in $e$, because $\mathrm{clip}$ is nondecreasing and the other maps are nonincreasing.

(iii) The floor, the nearest-integer and the ceiling conventions differ by at most one client, because $\lceil x\rceil-\lfloor x\rfloor\le 1$.

(iv) The original unrounded formula $C_{k_{\min}}+(C_{k_{\max}}-C_{k_{\min}})(1-\rho)$ exceeds $C_{k_{\max}}$ if and only if $\rho<0$.

(v) Since $m_t\ge C_{k_{\min}}$, the uploads over $T$ rounds are at least $T\,C_{k_{\min}}$, so the saving relative to a fixed cohort of $C_{k_{\max}}$ is at most $1-C_{k_{\min}}/C_{k_{\max}}$: 50% for bounds of 5 and 10, and 20% for bounds of 8 and 10. $\square$

**Lemma C (aggregation weights, Eq. (18); R1-03, R1-11, R2-07).** Let $q_i^t=s_{i,+}^t/H^t$ if $H^t>0$ and $q_i^t=n_i/\sum_{j}n_j$ otherwise, and $S_i^t=(1-\kappa)n_i/\sum_j n_j+\kappa q_i^t$ with $\kappa\in[0,1]$.

(i) $S_i^t\ge 0$ and $\sum_{i\in C_k^t}S_i^t=1$, since $S^t$ is a convex combination of two points of the simplex.

(ii) For $\kappa=0$, $w_{\mathrm{global}}^{t+1}=\sum_i n_iw_i^t/\sum_i n_i$; when the cohort is the whole population these are the weights $n_i/n$ of Eq. (1).

(iii) Negative scores: only the positive part enters. If no score is positive, or all scores are zero (identical client models give $\Delta KL=0$ and $\sigma^2=0$), then $H^t=0$ and the sample-count fallback applies, so no division by a vanishing quantity occurs.

(iv) For $H^t>0$ the scaled form $z_i/\sum_j z_j$ with $z_i=s_{i,+}^t/\hat s^{\,t}$ equals $s_{i,+}^t/H^t$, because $\hat s^{\,t}>0$ cancels. $\square$

**Proposition 2 (bounded waiting) and Propositions 1 and 3** are proved in Section 4.3 (part 3). They are also executed in part 6: the guard was simulated for 3,000 rounds with adversarial and random scores (rows H1) and the quantities of Proposition 1 were evaluated on random inputs (rows H2 to H5); 13 unit tests pass (`fedfacs_repro/test_spec.py`).
"""

EQ_NOTE = '::: {custom-style="BA-Note"}' + NL + "New or changed equations of Section 4.2 that the text above relies on. The numbers are those of the revised manuscript." + NL + ":::" + NL


def new_equations_md():
    t = B.REV
    out = [EQ_NOTE]
    want = [("tag{5a}", "5a"), ("tag{5b}", "5b"), ("tag{12a}", "12a"), ("label{eq:ck_selection}", "16"), ("label{eq:stability_norm}", "18")]
    for m in re.finditer(BSR + r"begin\{equation\}(.*?)" + BSR + r"end\{equation\}", t, re.S):
        body = m.group(1)
        for key, num in want:
            if BS + key in body:
                out.append("$$ %s \\qquad (%s) $$" % (B.eq_clean(body), num))
                out.append("")
    return NL.join(out)


def sec54_md():
    s = NL.join(l for l in B.S54.split(NL) if not l.lstrip().startswith("%"))
    s = re.sub(BSR + r"subsection\{[^}]*\}" + BSR + r"label\{[^}]*\}", "", s)
    out = ['::: {custom-style="BA-Sub"}' + NL + "5.4 Analysis of the selection score (new subsection)" + NL + ":::" + NL]
    pos = 0
    for m in re.finditer(BSR + r"begin\{table\}.*?" + BSR + r"end\{table\}", s, re.S):
        for p in [x.strip() for x in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", s[pos:m.start()]) if x.strip()]:
            out.append(B.conv_text(" ".join(p.split(NL))) + NL)
        lab = re.search(r"label\{([^}]*)\}", m.group(0)).group(1)
        out.append(TABLE_MD[lab] + NL)
        pos = m.end()
    for p in [x.strip() for x in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", s[pos:]) if x.strip()]:
        out.append(B.conv_text(" ".join(p.split(NL))) + NL)
    return NL.join(out)


def ledger_md():
    rows = ["| ID | Where | Claim | In the paper | Recomputed from the raw runs | Source |", "|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|"]
    esc = lambda x: str(x).replace("|", "/")
    for c in CLAIMS:
        rows.append("| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |" % (esc(c["id"]), esc(c["where"]), esc(c["claim"]), esc(c["text"]), esc(c["got"]), esc(c["source"])))
    n_ok = sum(1 for c in CLAIMS if c["ok"])
    head = (NL + "# 6. Ledger: every number of the new text, recomputed from the raw run files" + NL + NL +
            '::: {custom-style="BA-Note"}' + NL +
            "Method. `tools/verify_claims.py` reads the 683 result files in `fedfacs_repro/results/` and recomputes each value stated in Sections 4.3 and 5.4 and in the replacement files: means, paired differences with 95% bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples), Spearman correlations, rank AUC, waiting times, cohort sizes, aggregation weights and influence; the properties of Section 4.3 are executed on random inputs and by simulation. "
            "Result: %d of %d values agree with the text. Rerun: `python tools/verify_claims.py`." % (n_ok, len(CLAIMS)) + NL + ":::" + NL + NL)
    corr = r"""
**Values corrected by this verification (internal, not for the manuscript).** The text of the earlier drafts contained the following values, which the raw runs did not reproduce; each was replaced by the recomputed value and the sentence was rewritten around it.

| Earlier statement | Recomputed | Change made |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the mean mixing coefficient decreased in 96.7% of 1,827 rounds with $\nu>0$ | 98.2% of 4,316 rounds (96 main runs); the earlier alignment of $\nu$ with the round was off by one | value and alignment replaced |
| the coefficient settles at a median of 0.04 (mean 0.10) | median 0.10, mean 0.14 over the diagnostic rounds 5 to 100 | value replaced |
| $\Delta KL$ is typically much smaller than one; clients are grouped by waiting time | $\Delta KL$ has a median of 0.73 (F: 1.88); the weighted utility term is a median 3% of the weighted fairness term; the priority is rank-correlated with F (0.92) | the sentence now states the measured dominance of the waiting time, not a grouping |
| Jain index 0.995 to 0.998 for the sample-count aggregation | 0.995 to 0.999 | range corrected |
| rank-normalised priority: Jain 0.95 to 0.99, longest wait 18 to 20 | 0.94 to 0.99, 17 to 20 | ranges corrected |
| FedFACS-R accuracy difference −0.30 [−0.57, +0.05] and −0.08 [−0.56, +0.41] | −0.29 [−0.57, +0.05] and −0.08 [−0.55, +0.41] | rounding corrected |
"""
    return head + NL.join(rows) + NL + corr

    md = [HEAD, LEMMAS]
    md.append(NL + "# 3. New Section 4.3 (insert after Section 4.2, before Section 5)" + NL)
    md.append(B.section43_md())
    md.append(NL + "# 4. New Section 5.4 with its tables (insert at the end of Section 5, before the Conclusion)" + NL)
    md.append(sec54_md())
    md.append("Table W (supporting evidence for the paragraph on aggregation weights; not a table of the manuscript)." + NL + NL + WP.split("Table W.", 1)[1].split(NL, 1)[1])
    md.append(NL + "# 5. New and changed equations" + NL)

content.text:
الملف الموحّد جاهز: [FedFACS_Missing_Sections_5-8.docx](FedFACS_Missing_Sections_5-8.docx). لم أفتحه في Word، وفحصت XML فقط (228 معادلة و8 جداول).

## ما في الملف
1. **خريطة الإدراج:** كل عنصر جديد، وأين يوضع، وأي نقطة ومراجع تعتمد عليه.
2. **براهين** كل ما يقوله النص الجديد:
   - اتجاه المتحكم (المعادلة 8).
   - قاعدة حجم المجموعة: الحدود والتقريب والحد الأعلى للتوفير.
   - أوزان التجميع: غير سالبة ومجموعها 1، وتتحمل الدرجات السالبة والنماذج المتطابقة.
3. **القسم 4.3 كاملاً** بنصوص Propositions 1–3 وبراهينها.
4. **القسم 5.4 كاملاً** مع الجداول X وX2 وY وZ.
5. **المعادلات الجديدة** (5a) و(5b) و(12a) و(16) و(18).
6. **سجل الأدلة:** 56 رقماً. كل رقم يقابله ما أعاد السكربت حسابه من الملفات الخام، ومصدره. التشغيل: `python tools/verify_claims.py`. خصائص القسم 4.3 نُفّذت أيضاً بمحاكاة 3000 جولة وبإدخالات عشوائية.

## الفحص كشف 7 مواضع لم تتطابق وأصلحتها
- **"ΔKL typically much smaller than one" كان غير صحيح.** القيمة الوسيطة 0.73 مقابل 1.88 للحد F. الصحيح أن الأولوية يحددها وقت الانتظار لأن المتحكم يُبقي المعامل a صغيراً (وسيط 0.10): الحد المرجّح a·ΔKL يساوي وسيطاً 3% من (1−a)·F، وارتباط الأولوية بالحد F هو 0.92. أعدت صياغة الجملة في أربعة مواضع (4.2 وفقرة المتحكم و5.4 وملفات Word).
- **"96.7% من 1,827 جولة"** لم يُعاد إنتاجها. الرقم الصحيح 98.2% من 4,316 جولة في 96 تشغيلاً أساسياً. وكان ربط ν بالجولة مُزاحاً بجولة واحدة.
- **وسيط المعامل a:** كان 0.04، والصحيح 0.10 (المتوسط 0.14).
- **مدى مؤشر Jain** للتجميع بعدد العينات 0.995–0.999 (كان 0.998).
- **مدى مؤشر Jain** للأولوية المعيَّرة بالرتبة 0.94–0.99 وأطول انتظار 17–20 (كانت 0.95–0.99 و18–20).
- **فروق FedFACS-R:** −0.29 (أفضل جولة) و−0.55 (حد أدنى للفاصل في آخر 10 جولات)، كانت −0.30 و−0.56.

جدول بهذه التصحيحات في آخر الملف، علّمته "داخلي، ليس للمخطوطة".

## بنود مفتوحة
- **الفقرة الأخيرة من 4.3 (Scope):** تقول إننا لا نشتق معدل تقارب لـFedFACS، وإنه متروك للعمل المستقبلي. هذا يخص ملاحظة R2-18 ولا يزال مفتوحاً، ولم أغيّره.
- **الجداول X وX2 وY وZ:** ترقيمها في المخطوطة يتولاه LaTeX، والحروف في الملف للتسمية فقط.

ملفات 5–6 و6 و7–8 أُعيد بناؤها بالأرقام والصياغات المصححة.

content.text:
**Waiting-time guard** (حارس زمن الانتظار) هو قاعدة بتضمن إن مفيش عميل يفضل مستني من غير دور أكتر من حد معين. وهو المقصود بـ"waiting-time proposition" اللي سألت عنه، وهي Proposition 2 في القسم 4.3.

## الفكرة ببساطة
كل عميل ليه عدّاد: كام جولة عدّت من غير ما يتختار. العدّاد بيزيد 1 كل جولة لو ما اتختارش، وبيرجع صفر لو اتختار.

## القاعدة
- نحدد حد أقصى R = ⌈N / Cmin⌉. بـ100 عميل وأقل مجموعة 5، يبقى R = 20.
- أي عميل عدّاده وصل R أو أكتر يتسمى "متأخر".
- المتأخرين بيتختاروا **الأول**، الأقدم انتظاراً الأول، وعند التعادل بالرقم التعريفي.
- لو فيه مكان زيادة في المجموعة، الباقي يتختار بالدرجة العادية (fitness).
- لو مفيش متأخرين، القاعدة العادية هي اللي بتشتغل.

## الضمان (Proposition 2)
مفيش عميل هيستنى أكتر من **39 جولة** (بـ100 عميل وأقل مجموعة 5)، مهما كانت الدرجات. والبرهان في القسم 4.3.

## ملاحظتين مهمتين
- **الحارس غير مفعّل في تشغيلاتنا.** أطول انتظار فعلي كان 17 جولة (N=100)، أقل من العتبة 20. يعني النتائج المذكورة هي نتائج القاعدة العادية بدون الحارس. الحارس ضمان نظري لو حصل أسوأ سيناريو.
- **محاكاة الحارس:** شغّلت المحاكاة بدرجات عدائية (تفضّل العملاء اللي اتختاروا قريب). أطول انتظار كان 31 جولة بـ100 عميل، تحت الحد 39.

وده بيرد على ملاحظة المراجع إن "العدالة مجرد ميل مش ضمان".

content.text:
**Waiting-time guard.** For each client, the server keeps the number of consecutive committed rounds in which the client was not selected, denoted $r_i^t$ (Eq. 7). A client is overdue when $r_i^t \ge R$, where $R=\lceil N/C_{k_{\min}}\rceil$ is the waiting threshold. In every round, overdue clients are selected first, ordered by decreasing waiting time and, for equal waiting times, by ascending client identifier. If fewer than $m_t$ clients are overdue, the remaining places are filled by the clients with the highest fitness (Eq. 14). When no client is overdue, selection follows the fitness ranking alone. Under this rule, no client waits more than $2\lceil N/C_{k_{\min}}\rceil-1$ consecutive rounds, whatever the fitness scores are (Proposition 2).

**للتوضيح في الـ paper (جملة واحدة تُضاف بعده):**

> The guard acts only as a safeguard: it changes the selection only when a client has waited for $R$ rounds, and in all our experiments the longest observed waiting time remained below $R$.

**ملاحظات:**
- الحد الأقصى المذكور هو $W-1$ من Proposition 2 في [sn-article.tex](paper_overleaf_revised/sn-article.tex) (القسم 4.3)، وقيمته 39 بـ$N=100$ و$C_{k_{\min}}=5$.
- عبارة "remained below $R$" صحيحة في تشغيلاتنا. أطول انتظار كان 17 مقابل $R=20$ عند $N=100$، والأرقام للأحجام الأخرى في سجل الأدلة.

**الفقرة الطويلة تحت المعادلة 16** (بدل 8 جمل):

> When $\rho^{t-1}$ indicates sharp improvement the cohort decreases; it equals $C_{k_{\max}}$ when $\rho^{t-1}\le 0$ (stagnation or a loss increase) and in the first round ($\rho^0=0$), and it reaches $C_{k_{\min}}$ at $\rho^{t-1}\ge 1$. Intermediate values are interpolated linearly and rounded to the nearest integer, which changes a cohort by at most one client relative to any other rounding convention. Because $\rho^{t-1}$ is an absolute loss reduction, it kept the cohort at $C_{k_{\max}}$ in 75% of the rounds in our runs (Section 5.4). FedFACS-R therefore uses the relative efficiency $e^{t-1}=\rho^{t-1}/\Omega^{t}$ ($e^{t-1}=0$ if $\Omega^{t}\le 0$) in Eq. (16), so that a round that progresses at the reference pace selects $C_{k_{\min}}$ clients (Table Z). A candidate whose update is not finite is excluded; if fewer than $m_t$ candidates remain, all of them are selected.

> Here $L_{global}^{t}$ is the validation loss after round $t$ ($L_{global}^{0}$: initial model). A negative $\rho^{t}$ is a loss increase and is kept; a zero or non-finite previous loss cancels the round.

**جملة القسم 5.1:**

> Moreover, dynamic cohort sizing (FedFACS-A2) changes the accuracy only slightly and lowers the upload volume by the reduction of the mean cohort below the fixed size, 1.7% in our runs (bounds 5 and 10, Table Z); this saving cannot exceed $1-C_{k_{\min}}/C_{k_{\max}}$ for any configuration.

عدّلت الفقرة بدون أي أرقام، وكل عنصر فيها بيوضّح فايدته لنا. عدّلتها في [sn-article.tex](paper_overleaf_revised/sn-article.tex) وفي [FedFACS_Replacements_7_8.docx](FedFACS_Replacements_7_8.docx)، ولم أفتح Word وفحصت النص فقط.

**الفقرة تحت المعادلة 16:**

> When $\rho^{t-1}$ indicates sharp improvement, a smaller cohort suffices: the global model is improving quickly, so the upload cost of the round falls without slowing progress, and the cohort reaches $C_{k_{\min}}$ at $\rho^{t-1}\ge 1$. When $\rho^{t-1}\le 0$ (stagnation or a loss increase) and in the first round ($\rho^0=0$), the cohort is $C_{k_{\max}}$: averaging more clients reduces the variance of the aggregate and supplies more diverse updates, which helps the model to leave the plateau. Intermediate values are interpolated linearly and rounded to the nearest integer, so that any rounding convention changes a cohort by at most one client and the participation count is insensitive to it. The absolute reduction $\rho^{t-1}$ is small in our runs and keeps the cohort near $C_{k_{\max}}$; FedFACS-R therefore measures it against the reference pace of the run, $e^{t-1}=\rho^{t-1}/\Omega^{t}$ ($e^{t-1}=0$ if $\Omega^{t}\le 0$), so that a round that progresses at least at that pace selects $C_{k_{\min}}$ clients and the whole range $[C_{k_{\min}},C_{k_{\max}}]$ is used, which lowers the upload volume without a detectable change in accuracy (Table Z). A candidate whose update is not finite is excluded; if fewer than $m_t$ candidates remain, all of them are selected.

**جملة القسم 5.1:**

> Moreover, dynamic cohort sizing (FedFACS-A2) changes the accuracy only slightly and lowers the upload volume by exactly the reduction of the mean cohort below the fixed size (Table Z); this reduction is bounded by $1-C_{k_{\min}}/C_{k_{\max}}$ for any configuration, so wider bounds allow a larger saving.

**ما بنيته على الأدلة وما هو منطق عام:**
- **مدعوم بتجاربنا:** "الكفاءة المطلقة تُبقي المجموعة قرب الحد الأقصى"، و"الكفاءة النسبية تستخدم المدى كله وتقلل الرفع دون تغيّر دال في الدقة". الأرقام موجودة في الجدول Z وسجل الأدلة، ولم أذكرها في النص.
- **منطق معروف في FL وليس نتيجة قِسناها:** "مجموعة أكبر تقلل تباين التجميع". جاء كسبب لاختيار الحد الأقصى عند الركود، وليس كنتيجة قِسناها.

> Here $L_{global}^{t}$ is the validation loss after round $t$ and $L_{global}^{0}$ that of the initial model. Hence $\rho^{t}\le 1$: it is positive when the loss falls and negative when it rises, and a negative value is kept because it selects the maximum cohort. **المعلومات اللي فيه:**
- **$\rho^t \le 1$:** لأن $\rho^t=(L^{t-1}-L^t)/L^{t-1}$ و$L^{t-1}>0$ و$L^t\ge 0$.
- **الإشارة:** الموجبة معناها نزول الخسارة، والسالبة معناها ارتفاعها.

أعدت صياغة الجملة الأخيرة (القسم 5.1)، وحدّثتها في [sn-article.tex](paper_overleaf_revised/sn-article.tex) وفي [FedFACS_Replacements_7_8.docx](FedFACS_Replacements_7_8.docx). لم أفتح Word، وفحصت النص فقط.

**النص الجديد:**

> Moreover, dynamic cohort sizing (FedFACS-A2) changes the accuracy only slightly. Its saving in uploads relative to a fixed cohort of $C_{k_{\max}}$ is $1-\bar m/C_{k_{\max}}$, where $\bar m$ is the mean cohort, and it cannot exceed $1-C_{k_{\min}}/C_{k_{\max}}$; it therefore grows with the distance between the two bounds (Table Z).

**المعلومات اللي فيه:**
- **صيغة التوفير:** الرفع الكلي = مجموع أحجام المجموعات، فبالنسبة لمجموعة ثابتة بحجم $C_{k_{\max}}$ يكون التوفير $1-\bar m/C_{k_{\max}}$.
- **حدّه الأعلى:** $1-C_{k_{\min}}/C_{k_{\max}}$ لأن $m_t\ge C_{k_{\min}}$. وهذا من البرهان في الملف الموحّد (Lemma B).
- **الخلاصة:** التوفير يكبر كلما اتسع الفرق بين الحدين.

مفيش أرقام في الجملة، والأرقام في الجدول Z.

import re

B = chr(92)
P = r"C:\Users\0xRay\Downloads\paper"
PT = os.path.join(P, "paper_overleaf_revised")
rho = "$" + B + "rho^{t-1}$"

# 1) the paragraph under Eq. (16)
p = os.path.join(PT, "sn-article.tex")
t = open(p, encoding="utf8", newline="").read()
nl = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in t else "\n"
t = t.replace("\r\n", "\n")
i = t.index("When " + rho + " is large, the model is improving quickly")
j = t.index("\n", i)
new = ("A large " + rho + " means fast progress, so a smaller cohort suffices and the upload cost falls; a non-positive " + rho + " (stagnation or a loss increase) and the first round select $C_{k_{" + B + "max}}$, "
       "because averaging more clients reduces the variance of the aggregate and helps the model to leave the plateau. "
       "Intermediate values are interpolated linearly and rounded to the nearest integer, so any rounding convention changes a cohort by at most one client. "
       "Because the absolute " + rho + " keeps the cohort near $C_{k_{" + B + "max}}$ in our runs, Eq.~(16) can use the ratio $" + B + "rho^{t-1}/" + B + "Omega^{t}$ instead (zero if $" + B + "Omega^{t}" + B + "le 0$), "
       "which spans the full range and lowers the uploads without a detectable change in accuracy (Table~" + B + "ref{tab:cohort}). "
       "Clients whose update is not finite are excluded; if fewer than $m_t$ remain, all of them are selected.")
t = t[:i] + new + t[j:]
open(p, "w", encoding="utf8", newline="").write(t.replace("\n", nl))

# 2) drop the name FedFACS-R in section 5.4 (both copies)
for f in ("sn-article.tex", "section_5_4_selection_score.tex"):
    p = os.path.join(PT, f)
    s = open(p, encoding="utf8", newline="").read()
    s = s.replace("(FedFACS-R: the ratio $" + B + "rho^{t-1}/" + B + "Omega^{t}$ replaces $" + B + "rho^{t-1}$ in Eq.~(16))", "(the ratio $" + B + "rho^{t-1}/" + B + "Omega^{t}$ in place of $" + B + "rho^{t-1}$ in Eq.~(16))")
    s = s.replace("Relative pace (FedFACS-R)", "Relative rate")
    print(f, "FedFACS-R left:", s.count("FedFACS-R"))
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf8", newline="").write(s)

# 3) builders
for f in ("build_78.py", "build_missing.py", "build_final56.py"):
    p = os.path.join(P, "tools", f)
    s = open(p, encoding="utf8").read()
    s = s.replace("The efficiency can be measured against the reference pace of the run (FedFACS-R), which uses the whole range.", "The ratio of the loss reduction to the reference rate can replace the absolute reduction, which uses the whole range.")
    s = s.replace("With FedFACS-R the mean cohort", "With the ratio rule the mean cohort").replace("the relative-pace measure (FedFACS-R)", "the ratio rule")
    s = s.replace("Relative pace (FedFACS-R)", "Relative rate").replace("FedFACS-R uses the ratio", "the ratio rule uses the ratio").replace("FedFACS-R", "the ratio rule")
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf8").write(s)

# 4) marker in build_78
p = os.path.join(P, "tools", "build_78.py")
s = open(p, encoding="utf8").read()
a = '"When $" + BS + "rho^{t-1}$ is large"'
assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, '"A large $" + BS + "rho^{t-1}$ means fast progress"')
open(p, "w", encoding="utf8").write(s)
print("ok")

اختصرت الفقرة وحذفت الاسم R (FedFACS-R) من كل المخطوطة ومن ملفات Word. حدّثت [sn-article.tex](paper_overleaf_revised/sn-article.tex) وملفات Word الأربعة. لم أفتحها في Word، وفحصت النص فقط.

**الفقرة الجديدة:**

> A large $\rho^{t-1}$ means fast progress, so a smaller cohort suffices and the upload cost falls; a non-positive $\rho^{t-1}$ (stagnation or a loss increase) and the first round select $C_{k_{\max}}$, because averaging more clients reduces the variance of the aggregate and helps the model to leave the plateau. Intermediate values are interpolated linearly and rounded to the nearest integer, so any rounding convention changes a cohort by at most one client. Because the absolute $\rho^{t-1}$ keeps the cohort near $C_{k_{\max}}$ in our runs, Eq. (16) can use the ratio $\rho^{t-1}/\Omega^{t}$ instead (zero if $\Omega^{t}\le 0$), which spans the full range and lowers the uploads without a detectable change in accuracy (Table Z). Clients whose update is not finite are excluded; if fewer than $m_t$ remain, all of them are selected.

**الرموز بعد التبسيط:** $\rho^{t-1}$ و$\Omega^{t}$ (المعادلة 11) و$C_{k_{\max}}$ و$m_t$، وكلها موجودة في الورقة. حذفت $C_{k_{\min}}$ و$e^{t-1}$ والاسم FedFACS-R.

في القسم 5.4، صفّ الجدول Z صار "Relative rate" بدل "Relative pace (FedFACS-R)". والمرجع في الملفات الآن "the ratio rule".

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This directory contains materials for revising the **FedFACS** paper — "FedFACS: A Fair Adaptive Client Selection Framework for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning" — submitted to the *Journal of King Saud University Computer and Information Sciences*. Both reviewers recommended rejection with substantial revision.

## Files

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `original paper.pdf` | The originally submitted manuscript |
| `FedFACS_Reviewer_Comments_Verbatim.docx` | Full verbatim comments from Reviewer 1 (21 numbered concerns, R1-01–R1-21) and Reviewer 2 (23 numbered concerns, R2-01–R2-23) |
| `FedFACS_14_Before_After fixing comments.docx` | Revision companion: 14 specific before/after text replacements with cross-references to the reviewer concerns each replacement targets |
| `springer_submission/` (+ `springer_submission.zip`) | **Canonical revised manuscript**: `main.tex` (Springer Nature `sn-jnl` class, `sn-basic`), `sn-bibliography.bib`, `figs/`. Merges all 22 replacements. Not compiled (no TeX engine here); needs `sn-jnl.cls` and `sn-basic.bst` from the Springer Nature template (Overleaf). Red `\todo{}` markers are author-only fields (names, affiliations, funding, COI, contributions) |
| `FedFACS_14_Before_After_FINAL.docx` | **Current, concise paste-ready 14-replacement Before/After file** (After shortened ~30%, Declared box per replacement, highlighted Status/author actions, symbol renames J, Pi, X, Tx; main.tex updated to match). Previous: `..._COMPLETED.docx` (longer). Older description: (native Word equations): all 44 reviewer comments folded into the 14 replacements, per-replacement status T/P/O, coverage matrix and notation table. Supersedes `FedFACS_14_Before_After fixing comments.docx` |
| `FedFACS_Response_to_Reviewers_v2.docx` | **Current** point-by-point response (44 points: 22 addressed, 22 open), cites revised-manuscript sections |
| `FedFACS_Additional_Replacements_15-22.docx`, `FedFACS_Response_to_Reviewers.docx` | **Superseded** by the two entries above (contain inaccuracies, e.g. 25/19 count, garbled market-size note, notation claim); keep only for history |

## Working with DOCX Files

DOCX is a ZIP of XML. The workflow for editing:

```bash
# Unpack
cp file.docx file.zip && unzip -q file.zip -d unpacked/

# Merge fragmented runs so text is searchable (run before editing)
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/

# Edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print

# Repack
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -XrD ../out.docx .)
```

The `scripts/` referenced above are in the docx skill's base directory. When adding tracked changes (redlines), wrap insertions in `<w:ins>` and deletions in `<w:del>`/`<w:delText>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes.

## Reviewer Comment Mapping Convention

The Before/After document uses this reference scheme:
- **R1-01–R1-21**: Reviewer 1's 21 substantive paragraphs in original order
- **R2-01–R2-23**: Reviewer 2's numbered concerns

## Core Technical Issues Requiring Resolution

The 14 replacements address these principal defects:

**Mathematical errors (must fix before resubmission):**
- **Eq. 7 (idle counter)**: Original rule never increments the counter for unselected clients — counter stays zero, breaking the entire fairness mechanism. Fix: unselected clients increment by 1; selected clients reset to 0.
- **Eq. 8 (control law)**: Denominator `λF + ν(ΔKL − F)` can be zero or negative. Fix: use `λF` (always positive since F ≥ 1) as denominator.
- **Eqs. 13/17–18 (aggregation weights)**: Raw stability scores `s = ΔKL − μσ²` can be negative, yielding negative aggregation weights. Fix: use positive-part normalization with sample-count fallback.
- **Eq. 16 (cohort size)**: Can produce non-integer values and values outside `[C_kmin, C_kmax]` when validation loss increases. Fix: add clamping and half-up rounding.

**Conceptual issues:**
- **Communication efficiency claim**: All N candidates download the model and train locally — only uploads are reduced. The original text claimed full communication savings. Fix: explicitly state that download, training, and scoring costs apply to all candidates.
- **Reference trajectory (Eq. 11)**: Original used a prior run of a competing baseline — unavailable in practice and circular. Fix: use a causal self-reference from prior FedFACS rounds with EMA smoothing (`β_ref = 0.9`).
- **KL utility interpretation**: ΔKL measures post-training divergence between local and global predictions, not a before/after reduction or evidence of improvement. Text must reflect this.

**Numerical inconsistencies to correct:**
- FMNIST Scenario 2 accuracy: 83.80% (not 83.08% as stated in one discussion location)
- Configuration B uses Pow-D (not FedProx) — baseline name must be consistent in text, tables, and figures
- FMNIST-S2 round reduction: 2.78% (not 2.2%)
- Table 4 F1/recall values for CIFAR-10 and FMNIST need reconciliation (F1 exceeds recall by 4–10 points, which is implausible for macro-averages)
- Table 5 COVID-19 average cohort (≈10.17) slightly exceeds the stated cap of m=10 — Configuration B bounds must be disclosed

## Status

Strict coverage of the 44 reviewer comments (Before/After FINAL, Appendix A): 24 resolved by text today (55%); 18 have corrected text with evidence in progress; 2 blocked on author inputs. Projected when the running experiments finish: 94% overall, every replacement >= 80% except Replacement 14 (62%), which needs the Zhai et al. and AHIBCS PDFs (Springer full texts not accessible). Nothing was fabricated.

**Experiments** live in `fedfacs_repro/` (v2 simulator: gradient clipping at 50 after a real NaN divergence at lr 0.05, failed-update exclusion, staged commit, confusion matrices). ONE sequential detached chain runs plan_main_a -> abl -> noise -> sens -> scale -> main_b (logs seq*.log; ~13-15 h); then plan_extra (FairFedCS, Greedy). Never run workers in parallel (GPU time-slicing made it slower). `python analyze.py` writes tables to `analysis/`. An hourly cron (session-only) monitors and restarts.

**Findings so far:** the method the manuscript calls "FedFairCS" is FairFedCS (arXiv 2307.10738); a 4-round pilot showed fixed vs controlled mixing identical (fairness term dominates, as Reviewer 2 argued); a 100-round pilot showed FedFACS ~10x download/compute for near-perfect participation fairness and ~equal accuracy.

**Authors still need to:** send Zhai et al. 2024 and AHIBCS PDFs; optionally provide the COVID-19 Kaggle data; confirm release statement; fill author/funding/COI fields; verify refs `mukhtiar2025b` and `huang2020`.

- [Fix, don't just admit](feedback_fix_not_admit.md) — close reviewer comments with a real fix + declaration, Springer Q1 format
- [No fabricated numbers](feedback_no_fabrication.md) — never adjust/predict results to favour FedFACS; real runs only

       "because averaging more clients reduces the variance of the aggregate and helps the model to leave the plateau. "
       "Intermediate values are interpolated linearly and rounded to the nearest integer, so any rounding convention changes a cohort by at most one client. "
       "Because the absolute " + rho + " keeps the cohort near $C_{k_{" + B + "max}}$ in our runs, Eq.~(16) can use the ratio $" + B + "rho^{t-1}/" + B + "Omega^{t}$ instead (zero if $" + B + "Omega^{t}" + B + "le 0$), "
       "which spans the full range and lowers the uploads without a detectable change in accuracy (Table~" + B + "ref{tab:cohort}). "
       "Clients whose update is not finite are excluded; if fewer than $m_t$ remain, all of them are selected.")
t = t[:i] + new + t[j:]
open(p, "w", encoding="utf8", newline="").write(t.replace("\n", nl))

# 2) drop the name FedFACS-R in section 5.4 (both copies)
for f in ("sn-article.tex", "section_5_4_selection_score.tex"):

    s = s.replace("Relative pace (FedFACS-R)", "Relative rate")
    print(f, "FedFACS-R left:", s.count("FedFACS-R"))
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf8", newline="").write(s)

# 3) builders
for f in ("build_78.py", "build_missing.py", "build_final56.py"):
    p = os.path.join(P, "tools", f)
    s = open(p, encoding="utf8").read()
    s = s.replace("The efficiency can be measured against the reference pace of the run (FedFACS-R), which uses the whole range.", "The ratio of the loss reduction to the reference rate can replace the absolute reduction, which uses the whole range.")
    s = s.replace("With FedFACS-R the mean cohort", "With the ratio rule the mean cohort").replace("the relative-pace measure (FedFACS-R)", "the ratio rule")
    s = s.replace("Relative pace (FedFACS-R)", "Relative rate").replace("FedFACS-R uses the ratio", "the ratio rule uses the ratio").replace("FedFACS-R", "the ratio rule")
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf8").write(s)

# 4) marker in build_78
p = os.path.join(P, "tools", "build_78.py")
s = open(p, encoding="utf8").read()
a = '"When $" + BS + "rho^{t-1}$ is large"'
assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, '"A large $" + BS + "rho^{t-1}$ means fast progress"')
open(p, "w", encoding="utf8").write(s)
print("ok")

- browser-automation: Load a web page in a headless browser and check what actually rendered — console errors, failed network requests, the DOM, and a screenshot you look at. Use it to verify your own web work before you say it is done, instead of asking the user to look at the screen. Triggers on: check the page, does it render, verify the UI, QA the app, is it broken, console errors, did my change work.
- game-development: Run the game and look at it instead of reading source or asking the user what happened. Use when a game or mod crashes, fails to load, or renders wrong; when you are about to start a game or game server from the terminal; or when you need to see a frame. Any engine: if detect finds no preset, write the three-field manifest (launch, log, sourceRoots) and run.
- research: Use the ContextPilot Research Gateway when bug-hunting with external sources — fetching web/doc pages, PDFs, or GitHub issues/PRs, searching the open web, or when a page/thread is large. Prefer it over raw WebFetch/WebSearch to keep context small while preserving exact errors and full source.
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask.
